articles.title: Voiture électrique : les ventes s'envolent en Europe durant le mois d'août
articles.text:
La voiture électrique vit une superbe période actuellement sur le Vieux Continent. Ses ventes ont ainsi explosé chez nous durant le mois dernier.
On n'est pas étonné en ce moment de voir la popularité des véhicules électriques. Avec la crise de l'énergie et les prix à la pompe qui s'envolent, à la suite des problèmes au Moyen-Orient, tous ceux qui hésitaient à sauter le pas ont enfin trouvé l'incitation qu'il fallait. On a ainsi vu les ventes de ces véhicules exploser en France au mois d'août. Et c'est partout pareil en Europe !
Les ventes de véhicules électriques augmentent de 52,2% sur un an en Europe
Mieux vaut de l'électrique en ce moment quand on est un constructeur qui distribue en Europe. En effet, lors du mois d'août dernier, le marché automobile agglomérant l'Union européenne, le Royaume-Uni et l'EFTA a bénéficié d'une croissance de 5,3% par rapport à la même période l'an dernier, à 832 637 unités.
Mais à l'intérieur, c'est surtout les voitures électriques qui se sont taillées la part du lion, représentant à elle seules le mois dernier 29% des ventes européennes. Avec 243 207 immatriculations neuves, c'est ainsi une croissance folle de 52,2% sur un an qui est enregistrée.
Tesla survole le classement, devant Skoda et BMW
La motorisation la plus vendue reste l'hybride classique, qui, à 273 266 unités sur le mois dernier, n'est plus si devant les véhicules électriques que ça. Derrière ceux-ci, c'est l'hybride rechargeable qui se taille une belle place, avec 94 133 unités écoulées (soit une croissance de +13,5%).
Les motorisations traditionnelles elles voient leur part de marché reculer nettement, que ce soit l'essence, avec une baisse de 23,5% (154 345 unités) ou bien le diesel, qui ferme la marche avec un recul de 23,1% (48 586 unités).
Pour ce qui est des modèles 100% électriques préférés des Européens, le top 3 est le suivant pour août 2026 :
- Tesla Model Y (10 281 immatriculations) ;
- Skoda Elroq (9 289 immatriculations) ;
- BMW iX1 (6 635 immatriculations).

articles.title: Meta's new smart glasses skip the cameras, and the privacy backlash that came with them
articles.text:
In a nutshell: Meta's Connect 2026 event aimed to address two of the biggest obstacles facing wearable smart devices: privacy for smart glasses and the size of VR and AR devices. The company's upcoming audio-only AI glasses look to put a digital assistant on the wearer's face while avoiding the surveillance concerns that have dogged previous models. Meanwhile, the company's latest VR device directly calls out Apple's failed Vision Pro.
Pre-orders are now open for Meta's recently revealed Ray-Ban Audio glasses. Starting at $349 and shipping October 13, the glasses handle music, calls, and AI functions without cameras. Meta also unveiled a VR headset that packs immersive media and productivity functionality into a form factor only slightly larger than a pair of glasses.
Meta compares the Ray-Ban Audio's functionality to advanced earbuds such as Apple's AirPods. Wearers can listen to music or podcasts, take calls, and chat with the company's AI assistant, Muse, with up to 12 hours of battery life. Muse only begins listening when users say "Hey Meta" or press the action button.
Although the Connect 2026 keynote did not highlight the fact that the Ray-Ban Meta Audio glasses don't include cameras, the omission is clearly an attempt to sidestep concerns about the privacy violations associated with camera-equipped smart glasses.
Earlier this year, New York banned such devices from courtrooms due to their recording capabilities, and Apple reportedly delayed its planned smart glasses as it wrestles with the issue. It remains unclear whether limiting smart glasses recording to audio will alleviate critics' concerns.
However, Meta has not given up on camera-based smart glasses, as the Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3 glasses are available today. Starting at $449, they include a new six-microphone array that dampens background noise by more than 90% and a 12MP camera for 3K video recording. Later this year, the glasses will even be able to record 360-degree video with Dolby Atmos spatial sound.
Meta also revealed new features coming to Ray-Ban Display. Starting later this month, users can activate turn-by-turn cycling directions with voice commands. Furthermore, instead of simply using street names, directions will describe the world around wearers to make navigation more intuitive.
Later this fall, WhatsApp and Meta AI app users in the US can show call recipients photorealistic avatars while wearing Meta glasses. The holograms use AI to determine facial expressions based on users' speech.
Meta VR glasses are coming next spring, starting at $1,299. Like Apple's Vision Pro headset, Meta VR glasses can display multiple virtual screens around the wearer, showing content from productivity and streaming apps. With 5K micro-OLED panels delivering 37 pixels per degree, Meta's device achieves the glasses-like form factor VR headsets have long strived for, weighing only 100 grams – about one-eighth as much as a Vision Pro.
Wearers can control a virtual keyboard, trackpad, remote, or game controller using gestures. Meta VR glasses will support Xbox Cloud Gaming and more than 75 VR games on day one that do not require controllers. The company is also collaborating with ESPN, Amazon Prime Video, YouTube, DirecTV, Crunchyroll, Plex, Peacock, HBO, Paramount+, and IMAX to deliver immersive, high-resolution streaming content.
Taking another shot at Apple, the glasses will also show a full-body hologram to call recipients instead of just a head and shoulders.

articles.title: Dataiku debuts cross-platform Agent Management, expands Cobuild building agent - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Dataiku debuts cross-platform Agent Management, expands Cobuild building agent
Enterprise artificial intelligence platform company Dataiku Inc. today launched Agent Management, a standalone product that finds and tracks every AI agent a business runs, including those built on other vendors’ platforms.
Dataiku also expanded Cobuild, its natural-language agent for building AI projects.
Agent Management is aimed at a gap in how large companies keep track of what they run. Most maintain a record of who owns each piece of software and when its license renews, and Dataiku argues that almost none can produce the same for their agents. Fewer than one in five organizations keep a complete and current inventory of their AI systems, according to research from IBM Corp. cited by the company.
A bank can say how many servers it runs “to the decimal,” said Florian Douetteau, co-founder and chief executive of Dataiku. Ask the same bank about its AI agents and the answer is “a shrug or a guess,” he said.
Once connected to the platforms where a company’s agents run, the software pulls them into a single inventory. Connectors cover Salesforce Inc.’s Agentforce and the agent services run by Amazon Web Services Inc., Microsoft Corp. and Google LLC. Agents built on Databricks Inc. or Snowflake Inc. show up too, as do Dataiku’s own, and custom environments can report in through the OpenTelemetry standard.
Each entry maps the tools and models an agent depends on so supervisors can see how it works. The riskiest agents carry a standing record of certification status and named risks. Tests on them rerun on a schedule, so an evidence trail is already in place when an auditor or regulator asks for one.
Dataiku is positioning the product against monitoring tools built into a single vendor’s stack, which it argues tend to favor that vendor’s own agents. Sitting above every vendor’s stack lets Agent Management answer portfolio-wide questions, such as where risk is concentrated or which agents cost more than they return. Users can pose those questions in plain language.
Plain-language questions are also at the center of the Cobuild update. Dataiku made Cobuild generally available in June as an agent that turns a business request into a governed Dataiku project without code, and the expansion carries that approach across the platform.
A new feature called Cobuild Insights lets any employee ask a question of governed company data and get what Dataiku describes as analyst-quality answers. Users can then take the same line of questioning into deeper data work inside Dataiku.
A second addition, Dataiku Headless, brings Cobuild to developers inside the coding agents they already use, such as Anthropic PBC’s Claude Code, OpenAI Group PBC’s Codex and Space Exploration Technologies Corp.’s Cursor. From inside those tools, a developer can build or change pipelines, models and agents.
Migration is another use. Dataiku said an old Microsoft Excel workbook or Alteryx Inc. workflow can be converted into a governed project, and the tool can also be pointed at a live environment to investigate problems.
Cobuild is also built into Agent Management, so a team can have it recommend business-value metrics for an agent or diagnose and fix a risk alert. Cobuild’s AI Catalog is growing to cover all of a company’s vetted assets, semantic models included. Users can describe a business need and have Cobuild assemble the approved assets that fit into an answer or a visual pipeline with full lineage.
Clément Stenac, Dataiku’s co-founder and chief technology officer, said enterprises tend to run technical and business teams on separate platforms “without shared data or shared guardrails.” A few pilots could live with that, he said. At scale, he argued, it becomes “a liability companies have to prepare for.”
Dataiku gave timing and pricing only for Agent Management, which will be generally available in October. Access will carry an annual per-instance fee, with monitoring metered by the agent.
The company also published the “Global AI Confessions Report: CIO Edition, 2026,” at its Succeed conference in New York today. The report is built on a survey of 685 chief information officers that The Harris Poll ran for Dataiku July 9-29 at businesses with more than $500 million in annual revenue in eight countries.
Nine in 10 respondents said they were confident they had complete tracking of their agents. Asked specifically about agents built outside approved systems or formal channels, 81% said they lacked complete oversight.
Employees are building agents and applications faster than the information technology organization can govern them, according to 84% of respondents. Most of the CIOs also believe their careers will be shaped by their success with AI, and 76% said their role would be at risk if their company failed to show measurable business gains from AI by the end of 2027. Their AI budgets are exposed sooner, and 72% expect cuts or a freeze if this year’s performance targets are missed.

articles.title: Apple vai corrigir bug que trava e reinicia o iPhone 18 Pro • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Apple vai corrigir bug que trava e reinicia o iPhone 18 Pro
Atualização deve ser liberada na próxima semana. Falha faz aparelhos reiniciarem após Face ID não reconhecer o rosto.
A Apple prepara uma atualização de software para corrigir o bug que faz alguns iPhone 18 Pro e iPhone 18 Pro Max travarem e reiniciarem após falha de autenticação pelo Face ID. A correção deve ser liberada no início da próxima semana.
A informação foi divulgada pelo site 9to5Mac nesta quinta-feira (24/09). Os primeiros relatos do problema surgiram no começo desta semana e, inicialmente, levantaram suspeitas de uma possível falha de hardware nos aparelhos.
O problema aparece após um erro de autenticação pelo Face ID dentro de aplicativos protegidos. Nos testes conduzidos pelo 9to5Mac, o iPhone deixou de responder aos comandos por toque e reiniciou alguns segundos depois. O portal conseguiu reproduzir a falha ao tentar acessar o aplicativo Passwords com o rosto parcialmente coberto pela mão.
Também foi encontrado um registro de “panic” na seção de análise do sistema após a reinicialização. Esse tipo de registro é criado quando o sistema enfrenta uma falha grave que força uma reinicialização.
Ainda assim, o problema não parece afetar todos os usuários do iPhone 18 Pro, mas relatos de casos semelhantes apareceram nas redes sociais.
Antes da confirmação da Apple, alguns clientes chegaram a substituir seus iPhones por novas unidades por acreditarem que as reinicializações poderiam estar relacionadas a um defeito físico. No entanto, a troca não deve ser necessária, já que a empresa confirmou uma correção por software.
A Apple não informou exatamente o que provoca o bug, mas os iPhone 18 Pro e 18 Pro Max estrearam uma versão redesenhada do sistema Face ID. A câmera infravermelha passou a ficar posicionada sob a parte inferior da tela, perto da região ocupada pelo relógio na barra de status. A mudança permitiu reduzir em 25% o tamanho da Ilha Dinâmica.

articles.title: GMKtec Evo-X3 review: Strix Halo in a brand new suit
articles.text:
Tom's Hardware Verdict
With its 128GB of fast DDR5-8000 RAM and AMD’s potent Ryzen AI Max+ 395 processor there is a lot to like. The sleek and strong metallic Evo-X3 redesign is also welcome. However, the new price of this AI workstation is difficult to swallow.
Pros
- +Uses AMD’s powerful Ryzen AI Max+ 395
- +128GB of LPDDR5X-8000 memory on board
- +Can use up to 96GB as VRAM
- +USB4 and OCuLink ports are available
- +Excellent metal build quality
- +Quiet under load
Cons
- -Quite large and heavy for a mini PC
- -Sizable and heavy power brick
- -Just one USB4 port
- -Not enough video outputs
- -Price doubled since the previous gen Evo-X2 launched
Why you can trust Tom's Hardware
GMKtec already has an AMD Strix Halo mini PC in its stables, in the form of the Evo-X2. Now, just six months later, we have another AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 processor-packing mini PC from GMKtec in the labs. The obvious difference is that the Evo-X3 has a brand new chassis and cooling design, it also comes with 128GB of LPDDR5X-8000 as standard. Those are welcome changes. Half a year later, though, the price has basically doubled as seemingly every electronics product with RAM and NAND chips inside has been affected by the ongoing component shortage.
The result is a desirable computer that will offer strong appeal to enthusiasts who want machines with a large pool of fast, unified RAM, in a competently revamped case. But you will have to have quite a compelling reason to part with the $3,799.99 our 128GB/2TB configuration costs in mid-2026.
Design of the GMKtec Evo-X3 AI Mini PC
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
GMKtec has thoroughly revamped its Evo-X family with the new X3. Gone is the short-but-stout design, where we saw a plastic inner case sandwiched by some brushed aluminum. Now GMKtec has gone almost entirely metal, with the exception of a textured and vented soft-touch green plastic cap. This towering new design, which is over 14-inches tall with the base attached, features a metal CNC chassis. That body feels very strong, the panels seem thick, and the base is made from a matching material. Where the mini PC meets the desk, there’s a pair of broad padded rubberized feet that you stick on after unpacking and fixing the metal base on the device.
While still in mini PC territory, the Evo-T3 is pushing it a bit at roughly 2.7 liters. Its flat base is about 4-inches wide, which helps it stay very stable on the desk. There are no side feet, which makes running it on its side inadvisible. Users will also have to hide away the large power brick if they are after the cleanest minimal workspace.
GMKtec Evo-X3 specifications
| Processor | AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 (16C/32T), up to 5.1 GHz , 85W | Row 0 - Cell 2 | 
| Graphics | AMD Radeon 8060S integrated GPU (40 RDNA 3.5 compute units, up to 2.9 GHz) | Row 1 - Cell 2 | 
| RAM | 128GB LPDDR5X-8000 RAM (soldered) | Row 2 - Cell 2 | 
| Storage | Dual M.2 2280 PCIe 4.0 x4 NVMe SSD slots (2TB / 4TB options) | Row 3 - Cell 2 | 
| Physical Ports | Front: 2x USB‑A 3.2 Gen 1, 3.5 mm audio. Rear: 1x USB‑A 3.2 Gen 2, 1x USB4 Type‑C (PD 3.0 / DP-alt), 1x HDMI 2.1 , 1x OCuLink PCIe Gen 4 x4, 1x RJ‑45 2.5G LAN, DC‑IN barrel jack | Row 4 - Cell 2 | 
| Wireless | Wi‑Fi 7, Bluetooth 5.4 | Row 5 - Cell 2 | 
| Dimensions | Approx. 14.0 x 7.5 x 1.6-inches (≈ 2.7 L chassis) | Row 6 - Cell 2 | 
| Operating System | Windows 11 Pro, Linux compatible | Row 7 - Cell 2 | 
| Price (as configured) | $3,799.99 (128GB RAM + 2TB SSD) Use code GMKX3DP3 to get 5% off the prices listed on Amazon | Row 8 - Cell 2 | 
Ports and Upgradeability
GMKtec keeps the front of its mini PC simple with just three ports and the power button. In the top third of the tower’s facade, there’s a central green power button with a white LED ring lit when it is powered up. The middle third of the front is left plain, but the lower third has one USB 3.2 Gen 1, one USB 2.0, and a 3.5mm audio combo jack. I wish there was a Type-C port on the front, preferably USB4 or better.
Around the back it has a good variety of ports, but I wouldn’t describe them as numerous. You will find a USB‑A 3.2 Gen 2 port, a USB4 Type‑C (PD 3.0 / DP-alt) port, an HDMI 2.1 port, an OCuLink PCIe Gen 4 ×4 port, an RJ‑45 2.5G LAN port, and a DC‑IN barrel jack. Ideally, I’d like to have a full size DP port, as well as a second USB4 port, plus more USB-A ports. If I were to use this as a daily driver I think I’d need to connect a fast USB docking solution for the oodles of peripherals I like to have ready and connected.
Wireless connectivity seems adequate enough, with an M.2 2230 card inside providing Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 5.4. I had no problems with either during the test period.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Access to the components inside the GMKtec Evo-X3 is straightforward, but takes time as there are eight Torx-6 screws securing the side panel in place. Once they were all unscrewed I needed to use a guitar pick and a bit of gravity to tilt the heavy panel off. Removing of the panel allowed access to the two M.2 PCIe 4.0 x4 slots, one of which was already populated with a Crucial P310 2TB M.2 NVMe SSD fitted with a slim heatsink. In the opposite corner of the chassis I saw an M.2 2230 socketed MediaTek wireless card. There are no other internal user upgrade or repair options as the 128GB of LPDDR5X-8000 RAM is soldered to the motherboard.

Productivity Performance on the GMKtec Evo-X3
GMKtec describes the Evo-X3 as a machine that targets AI workloads, but first we ran through our standard mini PC benchmark comparison suite, which targets more general computing usage.
A brief glimpse at the tech specs of the X3 reveals that it has lots of modern fast CPU cores, supported by one of the best iGPUs, and plenty of RAM and storage. It should make light work of our productivity benchmarks, and indeed its 16C/32 core AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 CPU left its mini PC rivals eating dust, most strikingly in multi-threaded tests.

As we expected, the single core tests show the GMKtec Evo-X3 is a competent performer in the context of the competition in our charts. It isn’t the only Zen 5 machine in this race, so it doesn’t get a chance to dazzle yet.
Moving onto the multi-core tests is where the Ryzen AI Max+ 395’s 32 threads show their potential for real-world data crunching performance. For example, in Y-cruncher it completed its Pi compute in around 60 seconds. That’s twice as fast as its nearest competitor in our mini PC charts, the Beelink SER10 Max.
Rendering in Cinebench is also strong. In Cinebench 2026, the X3 scored roughly 7,300 points in multi-core. That’s over 40% faster than its nearest competitor, the Arctic Senza AI 370. Video transcoding performance is also in a new class, with the Evo-X3 crushing the competition, achieving around 24 frames per second.
For some added AI benchmarking stats, we did a few tests in Geekbench AI and LM Studio Bionic to weigh the GMKtec Evo-X3 against the Evo-T2. These are both machines with large unified memory pools by default and which the makers claim to be local LLM champs.
Using Geekbench AI with the ONNX framework and DirectML backend the Evo-X3 achieved a half precision score of ~37,100. On the Evo-T2 using the same options, a score of ~23,060 was achieved.
However, machines like the GMKtec Evo-X3 and T2 might be picked up by consumers to work with local LLMs considerably larger than most consumer GPUs can load. With this in mind, I ran LM Studio Bionic chat sessions powered by the new Qwen3.8 27B Q4_K_M model on both machines. To use this 27 billion parameter model as intended, a machine needs around 20GB of ‘VRAM’ of shared memory to avoid undesirable side effects like out-of-memory errors and slowdowns.
I prompted the same tasks on both machines then analyzed the logs and found prompt processing was pretty similar between the platforms, ranging either side of 200 tok/s. However, the AMD Strix Halo Evo-X3 far outpaced the Panther Lake Evo-T2 by generating responses at up to 28 tok/s, compared with around 8 tok/s at best, respectively. It would be possible to tune these LLM speeds for each machine, but I didn’t tweak settings for the comparison tests. With 128GB of unified memory in the Evo-X3, allowing up to 96GB to be dedicated to the GPU, even larger models can be utilized for the most capable local AI chatbots, agents, generation workloads.
During our demanding tests, the GMKtec Evo-X3 stayed admirably cool and quiet. All our tests were done with the default 85W balanced profile, as the system shipped. Owners can also choose to run this system in Silent Mode (54W) or push it to Performance Mode (peak 140W).
Gaming and Graphics on the GMKtec Evo-X3
The GMKtec Evo-X3 is pretty good at gaming, thanks to its powerful CPU and iGPU with lots of fast memory onboard. Remember, the Ryzen AI Max 395+ has 16 Zen 5 CPU cores with 32 threads, and its Radeon RX 8060S iGPU features 40 CUs and 2,560 shader cores – more CUs than a vanilla PlayStation 5. The capacious LPDDR5X-8000 memory pool has a 256-bit interface.
Before moving onto our standard synthetic and AAA PC gaming tests, I decided to run around in Star Wars Outlaws. I chose the High preset, at 1440p, and kind of enjoyed this game, experiencing a performance level of mostly between 60 and 90 frames per second. The graphics weren't anything special, but I noticed the game was using about 9GB of VRAM which could have meant dips and stutters on systems packing 8GB GPUs and using the same graphics settings. While the CPU usage was mostly under 20%, the iGPU was nearer to 90%.
Next up, our benchmarks include a trio of 3DMark synthetics and two iconic PC gaming standards. In the 3DMark Solar Bay test, which seems most appropriate to the mini PCs we have tested in 2026, the Evo-X3 left the competitors in the dust with over 50,000 points. It was almost twice as fast as the Panther Lake B390 iGPU, and about three times as fast as the Radeon 890M machines that came with fast dual-channel RAM (like the aforementioned Arctic and Beelink mini PCs).
In 3DMark Steel Nomad we got a respectable score of 2,132, and the frame rate reached 21 FPS. It was a similar story in 3DMark Speed Way, where the Evo-X3 managed a score of 2,046. For some context this Speed Way result still lags behind my Asus Zephyrus G16 laptop with RTX 4060 Laptop GPU, which scored up to 2,425.
Moving on to real AAA games, let’s check the data provided by the multi-scene benchmarks built into Shadow of the Tomb Raider and Cyberpunk 2077. The former scales well with processor resources and can still often look and run great on humble iGPUs. As for Cyberpunk 2077, it can really push even the strongest modern GPUs, so here we've used two settings to show how the GMKtec Evo-X3 can perform. I thought both these titles looked better than Star Wars Outlaws, too.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
The Shadow of the Tomb Raider High 1080p test resulted in an impeccably smooth 138 FPS on average, with the low of 126 FPS, on the Evo-X3. That’s a great score for a mini PC without a discrete graphics card. I was inspired to re-test at 1440p High, and the X3 still achieved an average 96 FPS / low 86 FPS.
In Cyberpunk 2077 the Evo-X3 managed to achieve 96 FPS using the 1080p High preset, with 1% lows at 78 FPS. This is certainly another candidate for moving up to 1440p and/or higher quality presets. CD Projekt Red also provides lots of upscaling tech (DLSS, FSR, XeSS) settings to adjust in this futuristic RPG, to try and get your sweet spot performance / resolution / quality setting dialed in.
Power, Heat, and Noise when using the GMKtec Evo-X3
When I left the GMKtec Evo-X3 to idle, my power meter measured wattages around 16W from the wall for the whole system. When the PC was pushed with simultaneous CPU and GPU benchmarks running, power draw seemed to peak at a little under 150W. GMKtec shipped this device with ‘Balanced Mode’ set in the BIOS, allowing the processor to consume up to 85W. The supplied 230W power brick had plenty in reserve, and it might need it in ‘Performance Mode’ where GMKtec says that the processor alone will demand up to 120W with peak power spikes to 140W.
System tools showed that during light activities like browsing the web, and typing reports like this one, the CPU temperature stuck around 42 degrees Celsius (in a 22 C room). Playing games for 30 or 40 minutes, the reported CPU temperature seemed to stay between 75 C and 82 C most of the time. The peak CPU temperature I saw was 85 C.
GMKtec’s powerful mini PC was a quiet operator at idle and under load. My measurements from about half a foot in front of the device show noise levels under 30 dBA at idle, which is very quiet and under the measurement threshold of my meter. Stressing the system with multiple CPU and GPU loads I managed to get nearly 37 dBA out of the system. This seemed an exceptional result during my testing, as most of the time the max noise level during benchmarks was nearer 33 dBA.
Software and Warranty on the GMKtec Evo-X3
The GMKtec Evo-X3 ships with Windows 11 Pro installed. Unlike its Evo-T2 brother, I found no pre-installed AI apps and tools on the X3. However, I note that the product page mentions GMKtec Claw and Wrangler as features. I installed LM Studio Bionic and Comfy UI for some AI testing, though.
GMKtec sells the Evo-X3 with a one-year warranty.
GMKtec Evo-X3 configurations
GMKtec sells only two Evo-X3 configurations in the U.S. Both machines feature the same processor and generous amounts of RAM. The only configuration choice is between a 2TB SSD (our model) and a 4TB SSD equipped model.
At the time of writing our 2TB configuration is listed at $3,799 but the product page says the price is normally $4,100. The 4TB model is currently $3,999, discounted from $4,349. We don’t know when the prices might get adjusted. Pricing for computers and devices with lots of RAM and storage is volatile right now.
Bottom Line
I was impressed by many aspects of the GMKtec Evo-X3 mini PC. Computing on a machine with so much RAM felt quite liberating. Especially when so much of it can be allocated to the system's iGPU. Moreover, the CPU and iGPU components of the SoC are plenty powerful for the compact form factor. I was also impressed by the X3's sleek design, solid build quality, and quiet operation.
No machine is perfect, though. For example, despite having a variety of ports available including USB4 and OCuLink, I felt there were not enough ports in total. To use this as my daily driver I’d feel pinched by the Evo-X3’s design offering just a single USB4 port, and one HDMI out.
The price is high, even considering the spec, but that's unfortunately common during this component shortage.
GMKtec sells its new Evo-X3 direct at the offer price of $3,799, as mentioned and linked above. At the time of writing we note that our GMKtec Evo-X3 128GB/2TB configuration is also available from Amazon U.S. at the same price, if you prefer.
If you like what you’ve seen of the Evo-X3, the nearest competitors that we have experience of are the Evo-X2, also from GMKtec, and AMD’s first-party, turn-key Strix Halo mini-PC. However, we know there are several next-gen Ryzen AI Max 495+ machines coming to retail soon. Depending on market pricing, configurations, design, and port selections of these refreshed ‘Gorgon Halo’ models, they might be worth waiting for. We saw Minisforum, Lenovo, GMKtec, Chuwi, and AceMagic with AI Max 495+ designs at IFA 2026 earlier this month.
Mark Tyson is a news editor at Tom's Hardware. He enjoys covering the full breadth of PC tech; from business and semiconductor design to products approaching the edge of reason.

articles.title: Five neat things we learned about Meta's first-ever VR Glasses
articles.text:
It was a big week for Meta.
During its annual Meta Connect conference, the company unveiled a suite of new products, including the VR Glasses, the camera-less Ray-Ban Meta Audio, a Canadian launch of the Meta Ray-Ban Display and more.
But naturally, Meta’s first-ever VR glasses garnered a particular amount of attention, and they were certainly my favourite thing that I saw at Connect. It’s pretty impressive tech, honestly, offering the full VR experience across entertainment and personal computing in a cozy 100g package and small tethered puck.
After my hands-on demo, I also got to attend a media roundtable with Angela Chang, Meta’s VP of product management. In a wide-ranging conversation, we learned a lot more about the making of the glasses and Meta’s long-term ambitions with them. Here are some main takeaways.
It’s built on the Quest architecture
Impressively, the small, lightweight VR Glasses use “the exact same OS underneath” as the much bulkier Quest, according to Chang. Not only does this mean that developers will be able to more smoothly develop products across Meta’s entire line-up of VR devices, but it means that the thousands of titles already in the Quest library will be available on the Meta Glasses. These join the dozens of experiences that are being crafted specifically for the VR Glasses, including around 75 games that can be played simply with hand gestures.
Of course, this also means that anyone looking to upgrade could carry over their catalogue as well. For someone like me who’s spent hours across both the Quest 2 and 3 over the years, that should help make for a more seamless transition.
No compromises, technical challenges be damned
Of course, it’s one thing to have these experiences be compatible, but it’s another to have them look and run even better thanks to beefier specs, including 2.4K micro-OLED displays and Qualcomm’s Snapdragon Reality Elite chipset.
But Chang says one of the biggest challenges actually pertains to point of view.
“Trying to find this perfect sweet spot between the field of view [being] wide enough, big enough to be compatible with the traditional Quest content, immersive content, not feeling like you have to basically cut off all the years of content that we have invested in, while small enough to fit in this glasses form factor,” she explains. “We tested many different fields of view, sizes, resolutions, shapes and whatnot, and pushed our team very hard to try to innovate around the display, the display and optical stack to really get to the sweet spot.”
Another big challenge, she says, was figuring out how, exactly, to connect the puck, given that it handles battery, storage and compute.
“There’s concerns around whether that’s going to get in your way, and so we have to really think through the user experience, both in seated experiences, but also when you’re walking around on mobile,” she says.
“How do you get the wire to be malleable enough, soft enough, even though it’s a custom optical cable with lots of data bandwidth going up and down, to just be like smooth enough so that it doesn’t tangle? But at the same time, gracefully be able to drape behind your back, so you can clip the puck onto your pocket and have the fan vents face up, so we’re not causing it to heat up in your pocket or in your bag?”
(It should be noted that my demo was at a stationary chair and desk, so outside of standing briefly to try out the new hand-tracking Beat Saber Flux, I didn’t get a feel for how intrusive the optical tether could be.)
It’s been specifically designed with airplane use in mind
As someone who travels a lot for work, I’m always looking for a variety of things to do on flights, especially when I get restless. For that reason, I was really intrigued to see Meta specifically citing being on a plane as a major use case for the VR Glasses.
Right off the bat, the puck will help with portable use since it serves as the power source, no outlet required. And, of course, its tiny form factor compared to something like the Apple Vision Pro is a huge benefit. But it’s the other features that are particularly promising.
For one, the virtual private movie theatre functionality is a nice change of pace from the often small (and sometimes completely absent) in-flight entertainment systems. And for another, the productivity features, which include a fully interactive virtual keyboard that lays out on a flat surface in front of you, provide an alternative to using your laptop on the painfully small sliding table on the back of the seat. (Or, in another example I posed to Chang, those classroom-type chairs with a mini table attached.)
As Chang explains, the size of the surface doesn’t really matter, but rather the positioning of your hand for calibration. She adds that the surface’s material and contrast are also important, with higher contrasts yielding better results. “But in general, we’ve trained even for white tables so that it works well,” she says. However, she did acknowledge that hand-tracking becomes difficult in low-light situations, so you might run into some issues if it gets dark on the plane.
Lots of opportunities for refinements
Obviously, any first-generation product like this leaves a lot of room for iteration. But something that’s particularly unique about the VR Glasses is that they’re fuelled by the puck, not the frames themselves, which suggests the possibility of swapping it out with different models of varying power levels. In theory, that could be a way to help offset the fact that this debut model costs US$1,299 (about C$1,800), as it’s easy to imagine giving customers more flexibility down the line.
When another journalist asked about this during the roundtable, Chang smiled knowingly.
“I like where you’re thinking. It’s certainly something that’s been on our mind. I think for this first generation, given that it was many leaps of innovation all in one go, we had to use a pretty proprietary interconnect on both the glasses and the puck side,” she says. “So it’s not easily interchangeable with other types of standard interconnects. So in future generations, that’s certainly our aspiration, to be able to have more standard interconnects between the puck and the glasses, so you can actually mix and match.”
Meta VR, including Quest, is here to stay
Given that Meta was all about the metaverse and Quest headsets not that long ago, it would be easy to assume that the company is largely moving away from VR. While these new glasses obviously feature that technology prominently, the company is also merging it with the smart glasses format that’s become such a focus of its business.
That begs the question: what does this all mean for Meta VR in general? According to Chang, it signals the future, which is paying off longer-term work.
“We’re pretty proud of the fact that, earlier this year, we basically transitioned to a sustainable business model for the VR business. Because we want to be in this business for a very long time,” she said.
She also notes that the Meta VR Glasses aren’t meant to replace Quest because they serve different purposes.
“The Meta VR Glasses is our vision for many years, working towards that general purpose computing platform where you can do many things on it. You can do many things really well on it [now], but it’s not particularly optimized for any singular use case,” she says.
“We just want to make sure if you like to do work on it, you can do that. If you like to watch movies on it, you can do that. If you like to take it away with you anywhere you want to go, you can do that. Whereas the Quest is truly more of a bespoke product for specific audiences, gamers, and for specific use cases, [like] gaming, fitness, dynamic motion type of immersive experiences. So that’s how we think about it.”
The Meta VR Glasses are set to launch sometime in spring 2027. Specific Canadian pricing and availability have yet to be confirmed.

articles.title: Thermaltake Unveils New SWAFAN UNIFY Series Fans with Single-Frame Design and Swappable Fan Blades

Thermaltake Unveils New SWAFAN UNIFY Series Fans with Single-Frame Design and Swappable Fan Blades
Thermaltake, a leading PC DIY brand for premium hardware solutions, expands its cooling lineup with the SWAFAN 240 UNIFY ARGB Sync and SWAFAN 360 UNIFY ARGB Sync PC Cooling Fans, available in black and snow editions. Featuring a single-frame design and swappable fan blades, the SWAFAN UNIFY simplifies installation and offers different airflow directions. Dual Infinity Mirror Lighting creates layered lighting effects and adds visual depth to the fans.
The SWAFAN UNIFY series integrates multiple fans into a single frame, reducing the number of cables and mounting points required. With a set of cables and four corner screws, the design makes installation easier while keeping the build neat. Featuring Thermaltake's signature swappable fan blade design, the SWAFAN UNIFY comes with standard fan blades pre-installed and reverse fan blades included in the package. This allows the fans to be configured for either exhaust or intake airflow while keeping the fan face forward for a consistent and refined appearance.Enhanced Cooling Performance
Built with a 28 mm thick fan body, the SWAFAN UNIFY series delivers strong airflow and static pressure for efficient cooling. With PWM control ranging from 500 to 2000 RPM, the standard fan blades deliver up to 58.13 CFM of airflow, 2.86 mm-H₂O of static pressure, and a noise level of 30 dB-A. The reverse fan blades provide up to 56.15 CFM airflow, 2.23 mm-H₂O static pressure, and 32 dB-A noise level, supporting different airflow configurations.
Dual Infinity Mirror Lighting
Dual Infinity Mirror Lighting on the fan hub and around the frame creates layered lighting effects with two distinct rings. The inner ring features fixed white lighting, while the outer ring offers fully customizable ARGB lighting. The ARGB lighting is compatible with 5 V ARGB motherboard software from ASUS, MSI, GIGABYTE, and ASRock.
Screw-Hidden Design
Specially designed rubber pads cover the mounting screws, creating a smooth surface across the fan frame. The design allows the ARGB lighting to stand out while maintaining a clean appearance.

articles.title: Waymo is scaling fast: Here’s what the fleet data shows | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Waymo’s commercial robotaxi ramp-up looks expansive, both in geographic reach and in ridership. And by almost every measure, it is — until you pay attention to where the bulk of those robotaxis are actually showing up.
The numbers over the past two years reflect the kind of commercial rollout you’d expect from a deep-pocketed company like Waymo, which spun out of Google and still counts Alphabet as its majority owner. In September 2024, Waymo was operating in just three cities — Phoenix, Los Angeles, and San Francisco. Today, it offers robotaxi service in 15 U.S. cities, with most of those commercial launches occurring in the past year. Ridership has skyrocketed, too, with Waymo now averaging 500,000 paid robotaxi rides every week.
But a closer look at its fleet shows a company concentrating its efforts in just two states. About 80% of Waymo’s roughly 4,000 robotaxis are in California and Texas, and Texas is where the action is now: Waymo’s fleet there has grown by nearly half in the past three weeks, fueled by a new Chinese-built minivan the company is betting will help it scale, even as tariffs drive up its costs.
The other 800 or so vehicles are spread across cities in other states, including Arizona and Florida, another burgeoning hot spot. Most are the familiar white Jaguar I-Pace electric SUVs, but a growing number are the new minivans — a modified Zeekr RT that Waymo has branded “Ojai.”
Waymo’s focus on California is no surprise. It is headquartered in Silicon Valley, and much of its early testing and development work was conducted there. Plus, a segment of the population there is inclined to adopt tech at its earliest stages.
The recent growth in Texas is more interesting. Waymo has increased its Texas fleet by 49% in the past three weeks, according to state vehicle registrations and data from the Texas Autonomous Vehicle Fleet Tracker. As of September 24, Waymo had 1,102 autonomous vehicles registered in the state.
Waymo first launched in commercial service in Austin through a partnership with Uber in March 2025, letting riders hail its robotaxis through the Uber app. Since then, the company has expanded its robotaxi services in Dallas, Houston, and San Antonio.
Waymo’s Texas fleet remained relatively static for most of the summer, inching up from about 600 vehicles in June to more than 700 by the end of August. Then came September, when the fleet surged, driven by an influx of new Ojai minivans, which now make up about a third of Waymo’s Texas fleet.
Expect that share to grow.
The Ojai robotaxi, equipped with Waymo’s sixth-generation self-driving system, is supposed to help Waymo reach mass scale. Its interior is built to withstand heavy use, and it comes with an upgraded rider interface and Google’s Gemini AI, which acts as an in-car assistant for riders.
Strip away that technology, though, and the Ojai is a minivan made by Zeekr, a brand owned by China’s Geely Holding Group (which also owns Volvo). The Ojai is built on Zeekr’s SEA-M platform, a shared vehicle platform designed for uses like robotaxis and delivery vans. The base Zeekr vehicles are shipped to the U.S. without any Chinese connected-car technology on board. Once they arrive, the vehicles are sent to Waymo’s Arizona factory, where they are outfitted with Waymo’s self-driving system.
The Ojai is supposed to drive down costs and ultimately help Waymo reach profitability. For now, though, tariffs are cutting any savings. Under current U.S. trade policy, vehicles built in China face steep import tariffs, raising Waymo’s costs for every Ojai it brings into the country.
Waymo appears willing to absorb that cost. New York-based research firm MoffettNathanson, which tracks Ojai imports using detailed shipping records, said in its September report that Waymo is on track to bring 5,100 of the vehicles into the U.S. by the end of the year.
Where will all those Ojai vehicles go? Texas is certainly on the list. But Florida, where Waymo operates in three cities, and newer markets like Las Vegas will likely see an influx as well.

articles.title: Samsung 990 : pourquoi ce SSD d'entrée de gamme vendu à prix d'or risque de vous décevoir
articles.text:
| Capacité de stockage | 1 To, 2 To | 
| Format | M.2 | 
| Norme | PCIe 4.0 | 
| Type de mémoire SSD | QLC | 
| Vitesse lecture | 7000 | 
| Dissipateur thermique | Non | 
| Compatible PS5 | Non | 
Nouvel arrivant dans l'entrée de gamme du constructeur sud-coréen, le Samsung 990 est un SSD interne disponible en version 1 To et 2 To de stockage. Il a pour particularité de solliciter des puces flash NAND de type QLC, moiins endurantes que les puces TLC trouvées habituellement dans le commerce.
Nouvel arrivant dans l'entrée de gamme du constructeur sud-coréen, le Samsung 990 est un SSD interne disponible en versions 1 To et 2 To de stockage. Il a pour particularité de solliciter des puces flash NAND de type QLC, moins endurantes que les puces TLC trouvées habituellement dans le commerce.
On ne le redira jamais assez, mais la crise de la RAM touche toute l'industrie de la tech ; celle des modules de stockage, non plus, n'est pas épargnée par la flambée des puces mémoire. Tiens, prenez Samsung : après l'inflation sur les PC portables et les smartphones, c'est la branche stockage qui prend cher. Elle se retrouve, bon gré mal gré, à devoir revoir sa gamme d'entrée de prix avec un nouveau SSD interne qui opère des compromis assez explicites pour un SKU commercialisé en 2026.
À commencer par le cœur de l'architecture d'un SSD ; les puces NAND flash sollicitées, non volatiles, car elles conservent les données lorsque le module est éteint, sont ici des QLC, ou Quad-Level Cell. Elles peuvent stocker 4 bits par cellule avec 16 niveaux de tension différents pour maximiser le stockage disponible. C'est considérablement plus que les SSD de type TLC (Triple-Level Cell), pour 3 bits de données par cellule et huit niveaux de tension, que l'on retrouve dans les SSD comme le Samsung 990 Pro. Ce qu'il faut retenir, c'est que les SSD à mémoire QLC sont plus lents et, surtout, moins durables que leurs compères TLC.
Si le Samsung 990 présente des débits théoriques tout à fait décents pour un module à interface PCIe Gen 4 (7000 Mo/s en lecture), on ne peut pas en dire autant de son endurance de 800 TBW et de sa garantie de trois ans, contre 1200 TBW et cinq ans pour le 990 Pro. Ajoutez à cela l'absence de cache DRAM, et ce SKU semble tout droit arriver de 2021. Tout cela ne serait pas dramatique si ce nouveau SSD de Samsung ne coûtait pas aux alentours de 200 € pour sa version 1 To et 360 € pour 2 To, soit des prix quasiment doublés à caractéristiques équivalentes il y a de ça un an. Une norme à laquelle il faut désormais s'adapter.
Notre protocole pour évaluer la taille du cache pSLC (le mode le plus véloce lors des gros transferts) consiste à écrire un flux séquentiel de blocs de 1 Mo sur l'intégralité du disque via AIDA64. Ainsi, on détermine à partir de quel point les performances atteignent leur plafond. Ce genre d'opération est rarissime au quotidien, tout du moins pour la grande majorité des utilisateurs, même lors de l'installation d'un jeu lourd dont les fichiers dépassent rarement quelques dizaines de gigaoctets. Ce benchmark est donc illustratif et n'est pas pris en compte dans l'appréciation finale.
Sans grande surprise, le Samsung 990 ne brille pas par la gestion de son cache puisque les débits d'écriture s'écroulent un peu avant d'atteindre les 10 % de sa capacité, avec une moyenne finale de 664 Mo/s.
Pour un module PCIe Gen 4, on ne s'attendait pas à voir le Samsung 990 atteindre de telles températures. Sur notre carte mère Asus ROG Crosshair X670E, le SSD atteint 116 °C sur les sondes internes lorsqu'il est sollicité à pleine bourre. Chaud dedans et chaud dehors aussi avec un pic à 106 °C observé sur notre caméra thermique Fluke. Pour éviter tout goulot d'étranglement thermique sur les performances, nous avons réalisé nos benchmarks avec le dissipateur thermique de notre mobo — nous recommandons logiquement d'installer celui de votre hardware.
Samsung ne se risque pas à de grandes envolées quant aux performances de son 990 et annonce simplement “jusqu’à 7000 Mo/s” de débits séquentiels en lecture. Sur notre benchmark CrystalDiskMark, le module affiche effectivement une moyenne de 7290 Mo/s en lecture pour 5861 Mo/s en écriture, soit des performances dans les clous... Sauf en Mix, qui, comme son nom l'indique, simule les deux charges de travail en simultané. C'est bien là que le 990 montre sa faiblesse face à la concurrence en PCIe Gen 4, même devant le choix “budget” de l'Exceria Pro.
Quant au test Random 4K, qui simule des opérations parallèles, il affiche lui aussi des valeurs à la traîne avec 871 883 IOPS (entrées/sorties par seconde) en lecture et 1 239 652 IOPS en écriture, se plaçant ainsi derrière le Samsung 990 Evo Plus.
Ces écarts s'équilibrent toutefois sur le test de copie manuelle, où le Samsung 990 fait à peu près jeu égal avec les autres modules sélectionnés dans notre comparatif. Seul le WD Black SN7100 sort (négativement) du lot.
Samsung inaugure l'ère post-crise de la RAM avec le le SSD 990, un entrée de gamme qui fait des compromis de conception évidentes, sans pour autant (trop) influencer les performances en débits. Néanmoins, son tarif de vente toujours particulièrement élevé le rapproche de certains anciens modules flagship, alors même qu'il affiche des défauts évidents, comme son endurance moins longue et une chauffe trop prononcée.
Tant que les stocks existent, nous recommanderons plutot de se tourner vers les modules Samsung 990 Evo Plus et WD Black SN7100, affichant tout deux des tarifs similaires pour une longevité bien meilleure.

articles.title: Why ITSM Hub in NZ Is Gaining Attention Among IT Teams - Tech Guide
articles.text:
- ITSM Hub in NZ is gaining attention because it combines service management training, consulting, and a managed service desk in one place.
- NZ IT teams can access globally recognised certification offerings backed by experienced ITSM professionals.
- Flexible learning options make training easier for busy service desk and operations teams.
- HubCentre adds 24/7/365 service desk support with AI-augmented capability.
- Consulting, labour hire, and implementation support help teams move from planning to action.
- Strong results, including high training objective completion, make ITSM Hub feel practical and credible.
Introduction
ITSM Hub in NZ is drawing interest because many IT teams want clearer service management, stronger skills, and support that goes beyond theory. Instead of offering only training, ITSM Hub brings together IT service management learning, advisory help, and delivery support. For teams under pressure to improve results fast, that mix feels useful and timely.
Why ITSM Hub Is Popular with NZ IT Teams
Many NZ teams need more than a course. They need practical service management practices that fit the way their IT service desk works day to day. ITSM Hub speaks to that need with training, consulting, and managed support.
It also appeals to teams focused on business relationship management and continuous improvement. With a broader offer across assessments, coaching, and implementation, ITSM Hub in NZ plays a useful role for organisations trying to build lasting capability. That becomes clearer in the next two areas.
Rising Demand for Modern IT Solutions
IT teams are being asked to do more with the same people. That puts pressure on the service desk, project teams, and leaders trying to improve core ITSM territory without slowing daily work. ITSM Hub stands out because it covers both capability building and hands-on support.
A simple example is HubCentre. It gives organisations a managed service desk with 24/7/365 cover, AI augmentation, and options shaped around user needs rather than a fixed model.
Teams are paying attention because they can get:
- service desk support that runs all day, every day
- best practice processes backed by certified staff
- implementation help when internal teams are stretched
- learning and consulting from one provider
Aligning with Current Business Needs
Not every organisation has the same gap. Some need sharper process design. Others need a clearer capability model, extra labour hire, or a roadmap that links IT work to business functions. ITSM Hub supports that reality with a structured approach.
Its consultants assess current maturity in areas such as ITIL, SIAM, and P3M3, then identify gaps and build an improvement roadmap. That helps teams see where to focus first instead of guessing.
For example, if an internal change programme has stalled, ITSM Hub can add contractors or delivery support so progress does not stop. This makes the service feel practical for NZ teams with limited time and capacity.
Core Benefits of Choosing ITSM Hub
The main benefit is range with purpose. ITSM Hub combines service management training, advisory work, and delivery support, which helps teams respond to business demand without juggling several providers.
That matters when you need best-practice guidance and real execution. From capability roadmaps to managed support, the offer is built to improve performance, not just pass on ideas. The next sections show how this helps quality and skills.
Enhanced IT Service Quality
Short answer: ITSM Hub can improve service delivery by combining assessment, guidance, and execution support. That direct answer matters for teams looking for a fast decision and a clear outcome.
In practice, the benefit comes from using subject matter experts who assess current maturity, highlight weak points, and map changes in a realistic order. That supports continuous improvement instead of one-off fixes.

articles.title: Sabotage chez Starlink ? Une station terrestre est victime d'un incendie, la Russie pointée du doigt
articles.text:
L’unique station terrestre Starlink en Pologne a été victime d’un incendie ce mercredi 23 septembre. L’événement est marquant, étant donné qu’il s’agit d’un point de télécommunication primordial pour l’Ukraine. Deux ministres polonais n’écartent pas l’hypothèse d’un acte de sabotage opéré par la Russie. Si un acte criminel est confirmé, cet incendie pourrait augmenter les tensions entre la Pologne et la Russie.
L’unique station terrestre Starlink en Pologne prend feu
Ce mercredi 23 septembre, vers 21 heures, un incendie a endommagé la station terrestre Starlink située à Wola Krobowska (Grójec), à environ 40 km de Varsovie. Il s’agit de l’unique station terrestre Starlink opérationnelle en Pologne. Elle gère la connectivité satellitaire dans toute la région, mais aussi en Ukraine. En effet, depuis le début de l’invasion russe en Ukraine, cette station contribue à assurer la connexion Internet des Ukrainiens. Des satellites survolant la zone s’y connectent également. Vous l’aurez sans doute compris, cet événement a une importante dimension politique.
Si aucune victime ni aucun blessé ne sont à déplorer, le tableau électrique, des antennes et le groupe électrogène de secours du site ont été endommagés. Cependant, à l’heure actuelle, aucune coupure Internet n’est à signaler. L’incendie a par ailleurs été totalement maîtrisé.
La piste d’une opération de sabotage russe
Il reste à déterminer l’origine de cet incendie. Le média RMF FM rapporte que certains pompiers qui se sont rendus sur place estiment qu’il s’agit d’un incendie volontaire. Le porte-parole des pompiers de Grójec a quant à lui préféré rester prudent en indiquant que la piste d’un incendie provoqué par un court-circuit n’est pas à écarter.
Krzysztof Gawkowski, vice-premier ministre et ministre du Numérique en Pologne, a estimé qu’il était impossible d’exclure l’hypothèse d’un sabotage. Il a également évoqué un incendie criminel et affirmé que le mode opératoire était, selon lui, clairement russe. Le ministre de la Justice, Waldemar Żurek, a quant à lui déclaré sur la radio RMF FM que le pays a « conscience des attaques hybrides contre la Pologne » et qu’un sabotage n’est pas exclu. Le gouvernement polonais travaille actuellement à définir avec précision l’origine de l’incendie. Précisons également que cette station terrestre Starlink est exploitée par Exatel, la société de télécommunications appartenant à l’État polonais.
Si la piste criminelle se confirme, l’incendie de cette station Starlink pourrait encore accentuer les tensions entre la Pologne et la Russie.

articles.title: Melhor VPN para iPhone: como blindar aplicativos e reduzir o rastreamento de dados • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Resumo
- A utilização de uma VPN no iPhone é essencial para proteger os dados de usuários, uma vez que o ecossistema restrito da Apple não impede a interceptação de informações em conexões abertas.
- A NordVPN oferece recursos de privacidade, desempenho e proteção contra ameaças, incluindo protocolos como NordLynx e OpenVPN e proteção contra chamadas fraudulentas.
- A configuração da VPN no iPhone é simples e pode ser feita por meio do aplicativo oficial da NordVPN ou da configuração nativa do iOS.
O ecossistema restrito da Apple consolidou a ideia de que o iPhone é imune a falhas de segurança. No entanto, embora a blindagem do iOS proteja o sistema operacional, ela pode não ser suficiente para os dados que percorrem na rede, que costumam ficar vulneráveis ao rastreio de provedores e possíveis interceptações.
É aí que uma VPN pode atuar. Ao criar um túnel criptografado entre o aparelho e um servidor remoto, ela protege o tráfego da conexão, oculta o endereço IP e amplia essa camada para aplicativos que não estão restritos ao navegador.
Por que usar uma VPN no iPhone? 📱
A segurança de um celular também depende da rede. Mesmo com recursos nativos de privacidade do iOS ativados, o tráfego da maioria dos apps de terceiros pode continuar exposto. Uma VPN adiciona criptografia ao tráfego e pode ser usada em diferentes situações:
✅ Wi-Fi público: ajuda a proteger senhas, mensagens e outros dados transmitidos em redes abertas.
✅ Aplicativos: a conexão VPN pode abranger diferentes apps, e não apenas o navegador.
✅ Viagens: permite escolher um servidor em outro país para manter a rota de conexão mais próxima da habitual.
✅ Privacidade: o endereço IP real fica oculto do serviço acessado.
✅ Redes restritas: recursos como NordWhisper ajudam a manter a conexão em ambientes com filtros ou bloqueios.
Conheça os planos da NordVPN para o iPhone.
Retransmissão Privada do iCloud e VPN: qual é a diferença?
A Retransmissão Privada do iCloud (Private Relay) pode passar a impressão de que o iPhone já conta com uma VPN integrada. Os recursos têm objetivos semelhantes em alguns pontos, mas não funcionam da mesma maneira.
A Retransmissão Privada foi desenvolvida principalmente para proteger a navegação no Safari e usa uma arquitetura com dois relays para separar a identidade do usuário do destino acessado. Já uma VPN cria um túnel para encaminhar o tráfego pela rede privada do serviço.
| Recurso | Retransmissão Privada do iCloud (Apple) | NordVPN | 
|---|---|---|
| Cobertura | Restrita prioritariamente ao Safari, consultas DNS e tráfego HTTP não criptografado. | Pode proteger o tráfego de aplicativos e navegadores. | 
| Visibilidade do Provedor (ISP) | O provedor de internet continua vendo o destino do tráfego dos seus aplicativos. | Oculta o tráfego da atividade do provedor. | 
| Controle de Localização | Mantém o país e fuso horário reais do usuário. | Permite escolher servidores em mais de 224 locais pelo mundo para alterar o IP de saída. | 
| Proteção contra ameaças online | O iOS utiliza o ITP no Safari, com foco em reduzir o rastreamento entre sites. | Antivírus Next Gen bloqueia anúncios, rastreadores e URLs maliciosas. | 
| Kill Switch | Não possui recurso equivalente. | Interrompe o acesso à internet em caso de queda da VPN. | 
| Monitoramento de vazamentos | Não possui recurso equivalente. | O Dark Web Monitor alerta quando credenciais do usuário aparecem em vazamentos. | 
| Arquitetura | Separa a identidade e o destino acessado entre dois servidores operados por empresas diferentes. | Túnel VPN com política no-log e auditorias independentes. | 
O que a NordVPN oferece no iPhone?
A NordVPN vai além da função básica de alterar o IP. O aplicativo reúne recursos de privacidade, desempenho e proteção contra ameaças em uma mesma conexão.
- Desempenho e rede: em testes independentes conduzidos pelo West Coast Labs em 2025, a NordVPN atingiu uma média de 817 Mbps, sendo classificada como a VPN mais rápida em comparação a concorrentes avaliados.
- Protocolos: a NordVPN utiliza NordLynx, NordWhisper e OpenVPN, com criptografia AES-256-GCM ou ChaCha20-Poly1305.
- NordWhisper para redes restritas: o recurso ajuda a contornar firewalls e filtros rígidos de rede, ajudando a manter a conexão em ambientes que dificultam o uso de VPNs tradicionais.
- Proteção contra chamadas: identifica números associados a golpes e exibe alertas antes do atendimento.
- Antivírus Next-Gen: bloqueia sites maliciosos, anúncios invasivos e rastreadores.
- Dark Web Monitor: alerta quando credenciais do usuário aparecem em vazamentos.
Como configurar a VPN no iPhone
A configuração de uma VPN no iOS não exige ajustes complexos no sistema. A ativação pelo aplicativo oficial é direta e automatiza a criação do túnel criptografado:
- Escolha a assinatura ideal para você no site da NordVPN.
- Baixe o aplicativo da NordVPN na App Store.
- Abra o aplicativo e faça o login ou crie uma conta.
- Autorize a configuração de VPN quando o iPhone solicitar.
- Toque em “Conectar” para iniciar a conexão.
Caso prefira não usar o aplicativo, o iOS permite a configuração nativa com os dados do seu provedor:
- Abra Ajustes > Geral > VPN e Gerenciamento de Dispositivo > VPN.
- Toque em Adicionar Configuração de VPN….
- Escolha o protocolo de conexão e informe os dados solicitados, como servidor, ID remoto, nome de usuário e senha.
- Toque em OK ou Salvar para concluir a configuração.
- Para ativar a conexão, volte à tela de VPN e ligue a chave correspondente.
Depois disso, o aplicativo passa a encaminhar o tráfego pela rede VPN.
Privacidade estendida a todo o ecossistema
A mesma assinatura pode ser usada em até 10 dispositivos simultaneamente, incluindo computadores com macOS, Windows e Linux, tablets e smart TVs. Isso permite manter a proteção da rede também em outros aparelhos usados no dia a dia.
A NordVPN também afirma seguir uma política de no-log, sem registro das atividades de navegação. Segundo o material, a política já passou por seis auditorias independentes.
VPN no iPhone é mais do que trocar o endereço IP
No celular, uma VPN pode cumprir um papel mais amplo do que simplesmente mascarar a localização. Ela adiciona uma camada de criptografia ao tráfego, pode proteger conexões de diferentes aplicativos e oferece mais controle sobre a rota usada pelo aparelho.
No caso da NordVPN, esse conjunto é complementado por recursos como servidores especializados, proteção contra chamadas fraudulentas, bloqueio de ameaças e monitoramento de vazamentos.
Conheça a NordVPN e veja os planos disponíveis para proteger seu iPhone e outros dispositivos.

articles.title: La IA conquista los videojuegos en Japón: casi el 90 % de los desarrolladores ya la utiliza
articles.text:
La inteligencia artificial generativa está ganando terreno en la industria de los videojuegos en Japón. Una encuesta realizada entre profesionales de compañías como Capcom, Sega, Konami y Square Enix, con motivo del Tokyo Game Show 2026, revela que el 85,8 % de los desarrolladores japoneses ya utiliza herramientas de IA generativa durante sus proyectos.
El dato representa un crecimiento considerable frente a 2025, cuando el 51 % de los profesionales consultados reconocía utilizar este tipo de tecnología en sus procesos de desarrollo. En apenas un año, la adopción aumentó cerca de 35 puntos porcentuales, lo que muestra hasta qué punto la IA se está incorporando en los estudios japoneses.
PUBLICIDAD
El estudio también refleja que su uso no se limita a experimentos puntuales. Del grupo de desarrolladores que utiliza inteligencia artificial, el 63 % asegura recurrir a estas herramientas diariamente, mientras que otro 22,8 % las utiliza de manera ocasional.
Para qué utilizan la inteligencia artificial los desarrolladores japoneses
La incorporación de IA generativa en los estudios japoneses está relacionada principalmente con tareas destinadas a mejorar los procesos internos de desarrollo.
Entre los usos mencionados aparecen la detección y corrección de errores, las pruebas automatizadas y la optimización de diferentes tareas de trabajo. De esta manera, la tecnología no necesariamente interviene directamente en la creación del contenido que llegará al jugador, sino que también funciona como una herramienta de apoyo para los equipos.
PUBLICIDAD
Uno de los aspectos más llamativos de la encuesta es que la mayoría de los participantes señala que descarta utilizar código generado por inteligencia artificial como parte de sus proyectos. Esto muestra que la adopción de estas herramientas no significa que los desarrolladores estén delegando completamente determinadas áreas de producción en los modelos generativos.
Además, los profesionales consultados aseguran que los resultados producidos por IA son revisados y modificados posteriormente por personas. La supervisión humana se mantiene, por tanto, como parte del proceso antes de incorporar cualquier resultado al desarrollo.
La productividad es uno de los principales motivos
Entre los beneficios que los desarrolladores japoneses encuentran en la inteligencia artificial destacan especialmente la eficiencia y la productividad.
Las herramientas generativas pueden ayudar a reducir el tiempo dedicado a determinadas tareas y acelerar procesos que anteriormente requerían una intervención manual más prolongada. Para los estudios, esta reducción de tiempos también puede traducirse en un ahorro de costes durante la producción de un videojuego.
PUBLICIDAD
Este factor adquiere especial relevancia en una industria en la que los proyectos pueden requerir años de trabajo y la participación de equipos formados por cientos de profesionales. Automatizar determinadas tareas permite que los desarrolladores puedan dedicar más tiempo a otras áreas del proyecto.
Sin embargo, los resultados de la encuesta también muestran que la expansión de la IA no implica necesariamente una sustitución directa de los trabajadores. Al menos entre los profesionales consultados, existe una tendencia a utilizar estas herramientas como apoyo y mantener la revisión humana sobre los resultados.
Japón acelera la adopción de IA en los videojuegos
El salto registrado entre 2025 y 2026 evidencia un cambio rápido en la relación entre los desarrolladores japoneses y la inteligencia artificial generativa. Pasar del 51 % al 85,8 % de adopción en un año supone que la tecnología ha dejado de ser una herramienta experimental para convertirse en parte habitual del trabajo en numerosos estudios.
PUBLICIDAD
El debate sobre el uso de IA en los videojuegos, sin embargo, continúa abierto. La tecnología plantea preguntas sobre la autoría, la propiedad intelectual y el papel que tendrán los profesionales en determinadas etapas de la creación de un videojuego.
Los datos presentados durante el Tokyo Game Show 2026 muestran, en cualquier caso, que una parte importante de la industria japonesa ya está incorporando la inteligencia artificial a sus procesos. La tendencia apunta a un uso centrado principalmente en mejorar la productividad y automatizar tareas, mientras la intervención humana continúa siendo necesaria para revisar y validar los resultados.

articles.title: Andhra sets 70% renewable energy rule for data centres, addresses water concerns: Lokesh
articles.text:
Andhra sets 70% renewable energy rule for data centres, addresses water concerns: Lokesh
The state is positioning Visakhapatnam as a major data-centre hub as it seeks to attract large technology investments and build out its digital infrastructure.
Andhra Pradesh is adopting a sustainability-focused approach to its planned data-centre expansion, including a requirement that at least 70% of the energy used by data centres come from renewable sources, IT Minister Nara Lokesh said.
The state is positioning Visakhapatnam as a major data-centre hub as it seeks to attract large technology investments and build out its digital infrastructure. Data centres, however, are typically energy- and water-intensive facilities, making access to reliable power and water as well as environmental sustainability key considerations for large-scale expansion.
Speaking at a fireside chat organised by the Public Affairs Forum of India (PAFI) here, Lokesh said the state was addressing the environmental implications of data-centre growth by focusing on energy, water and other resource requirements together.
"The first thumb rule is that a minimum 70% of the energy used by data centres must come from renewable sources," Lokesh said, referring to sources including solar, wind, pumped storage and battery-based energy.
The state is developing a data-centre cluster in Visakhapatnam and is also planning to address its water requirements through the Polavaram Left Bank Canal, he said.
Lokesh said the Polavaram project would help utilise water that would otherwise flow into the Bay of Bengal, with supplies being moved towards Visakhapatnam to meet the requirements of data centres.
The state is also incentivising data-centre companies to establish desalination plants, Lokesh said, adding that one company is already setting up such a facility.
Data centres can require significant quantities of water for cooling, raising concerns about their impact on local water resources as the state seeks to attract large-scale investments in the sector.
He said Andhra Pradesh was seeking to take a "holistic approach" to data-centre development by addressing energy, water and other environmental requirements together.
Such an approach would be critical for states seeking to attract and develop large-scale data-centre investments while addressing sustainability concerns, Lokesh said.

articles.title: Google Pixel Watch: Wie die Uhr künftig vor Diabetes-Anzeichen warnen kann
articles.text:
Google Pixel Watch: Wie die Uhr künftig vor Diabetes-Anzeichen warnen kann
Es war bereits angekündigt: Google startet mit neuartigen Gesundheitsfunktionen für seine Fitnesstracker, die es so bei der Konkurrenz noch nicht gibt. Der sogenannte Health Guardian ist für die Pixel-Uhren der dritten bis fünften Generation sowie das Armband Fitbit Air gedacht und kann mittels KI-Auswertung wichtige Informationen berechnen, die der Gesunderhaltung dienen. In der Google-Health-App erscheinen künftig Blutdrucktrends, Tendenzen zur Insulinresistenz sowie Messwerte zur Atmungsqualität im Schlaf.
Was die Insulinresistenz-Analyse leisten soll
Die Funktion wertet Körperdaten, die die Sensoren von Pixel-Uhr und Fitbit Air erfassen, über mehrere Wochen aus und soll schleichende Veränderungen des Stoffwechsels erkennen – ohne Blutentnahme. Insulinresistenz ist eine Stoffwechselstörung und gilt als Vorbote für Diabetes Typ 2. Nutzer:innen sollen dadurch mehr Kontrolle über ihre Gesundheit bekommen und früh gegensteuern können. Google stellt allerdings klar: Die Funktion dient nicht dazu, Krankheiten zu diagnostizieren. Sie sei weder ein Vorabtest auf Diabetes noch überwache sie den Blutzucker in Echtzeit. Forschende von Google Research haben dazu eine Studie im Fachjournal Nature veröffentlicht.
Die Wearables schätzen den Blutdruck laut Google „passiv“ anhand von Puls und Bewegungsmustern, über den gesamten Monat hinweg und auch im Schlaf. Eine Blutdruckmanschette oder eine Kalibrierung braucht es dafür nicht. Über natürliche Schwankungen informiert die App nicht täglich. Stattdessen zeigt sie am ersten Tag jedes Monats einen Überblick mit Einordnung. Nur bei auffälligen Veränderungen meldet sie sich zwischendurch. Die ersten Trendberichte sollen Anfang Oktober erscheinen. Damit die Auswertung funktioniert, müssen für die Insulinresistenz an mindestens sieben Tagen eines Monats Daten vorliegen, für den Blutdruck an mindestens fünf aufeinanderfolgenden Tagen einer Woche.
Atmung im Schlaf und Notruf bei Atemnot
Die neue Schlafatmungsanalyse erfasst dem Unternehmen zufolge Schwankungen der Atmung während der Nacht und zeigt jeden Morgen den Anteil optimaler Atemphasen. Einmal im Monat fasst Google Health die Werte in einem Bericht zusammen.
In ausgewählten europäischen Ländern – darunter Deutschland, Österreich und die Schweiz – gehört zum Health-Guardian-Paket außerdem die Erkennung von Atemnotfällen für die Pixel Watch 4 und 5. Fällt der Blutsauerstoff einer Trägerin oder eines Trägers laut Google „zu einem lebensbedrohlichen Abfall“, löst die Uhr automatisch einen Anruf beim Rettungsdienst aus. Das passiert aber erst, wenn die Person nicht mehr auf den Alarm reagiert. Zusätzlich informiert die Uhr hinterlegte Notfallkontakte. Auf den Pixel-Watch-Modellen 3 bis 5 sind die Health-Guardian-Funktionen laut Google kostenlos. Das rund 100 Euro teure Fitbit Air unterstützt die Trendanalysen zwar ebenfalls, dort gibt es sie aber nicht ohne Aufpreis als „Health Premium“ ab 9 Euro im Monat.

Pat Gelsinger-backed startup PicoJool raises $27.5M to boost bandwidth for AI clusters
A startup called PicoJool that’s backed by former Intel Corp. Chief Executive Pat Gelsinger says it’s ready to help ease the strain on artificial intelligence data centers after raising $27.5 million in early-stage funding today.
The Series A round was led by Socratic Partners and saw participation from Hudson River Trading. It brings the company’s total amount raised to $39.5 million. It follows an earlier $12 million seed funding round last November that was led by Gelsinger’s venture capital firm Playground Global.
PicoJool is trying to pioneer a technology called Vertical Cavity Surface Emitting Laser or VCSEL, which is a kind of semiconductor laser diode. It enables data to be sent via light signals through optical cables rather than traditional wire, enabling much faster data center communications. The startup, which has developed a number of optical chips and modules based on the technology, says they can drastically improve the performance and energy efficiency of large AI chip clusters.
There’s a growing appetite among data center operators for this kind of rapid and efficient connectivity. The more powerful AI models become, the bigger the clusters of graphics processing units and other accelerators are needed to run them. These days, the world’s largest enterprises operate clusters containing hundreds, sometimes even thousands of AI processors, which are constantly sending data packets back and forth to one another so they can work in unison to power AI workloads.
As a result, data centers are dealing with a tsunami of data, and it’s putting enormous strain on the traditional copper wire interconnects used to link all of those chips together. They simply cannot keep up with the bandwidth demands of the largest AI clusters, and they consume vast amounts of energy too, driving up the cost of running AI.
PicoJool founder and Chief Executive Al Yuen says his company can overcome this bottleneck by swapping out older interconnects for its high-speed 100G and 200G VCSEL products. It also offers low-power MicroVCSEL configurations including its 50G NRZ and 64G NRZ/PAM4 interconnects. According to PicoJool, the MicroVCSEL platform is based on a massively parallel architecture that aggregates bandwidth while dramatically reducing the energy costs of moving data around AI clusters. It provides a pathway for data center operators to achieve connectivity of up to 3.2 terabits per second of bandwidth.
“Reaching 200G per lane proved that the performance is there,” Yuen said. “Our focus is now execution. This funding allows us to expand our teams in the U.S. and Taiwan, qualify products with customers and move a complete portfolio from chip-level VCSELs and MicroVCSELs into AOC and NPO modules.”
PicoJool will also use some of the funds to accelerate its research and development efforts and grow its operations and sales teams, Yuen said. But the main focus now is on commercializing its existing technology. To do this, PicoJool is working with WIN Semiconductors Corp. and other chip foundries to prepare the 200G VCSEL for mass production, followed by its other products.
Gelsinger said he was attracted to PicoJool by its ambition and the fact it has a viable solution to the AI data center bandwidth bottleneck that has constrained AI deployments globally. “The network is the AI, and connectivity is becoming one of the defining constraints on performance,” he said. “The industry needs a solution that can increase bandwidth while sharply improving power and cost.”
