articles.title: What Is JSA Construction Software and Why Every Site Needs It - Tech Guide
articles.text:
- JSA construction software helps you complete job safety analysis faster and keep job safety records current on active sites.
- It supports hazard identification by guiding teams through each job step and matching risks with control measures.
- Digital JSA software reduces lost paper forms, delays, and messy safety analysis handovers between crews.
- Mobile access lets team members create, review, sign, and update safety documentation on site.
- Built-in templates, checklists, and review flows improve consistency across construction sites in Australia.
- Better records and clearer safety processes help support workplace safety, compliance, and safer work every day.
Introduction
JSA construction software lets you do job safety analysis faster. You don’t need to chase paperwork across the site. Your team can handle job safety, updates, and sign-offs in one digital tool. This is good for construction safety because risks can change quickly. Your safety documentation can keep up and be ready in time.
Understanding JSA Construction Software for Australian Sites
JSA construction software lets you write down how a job will be done in a safe manner. The main aim of a job safety analysis is to split work into small steps, find things that may harm people, and list control measures before you start working.
On construction sites in Australia, this makes safety documentation clearer. It also helps make sure that how you plan to do the job matches what happens on site. The JSA construction software guides you, keeps job safety records, and lets you update these records quickly when site conditions change.
What Is a Job Safety Analysis (JSA) in Construction?
A job safety analysis identifies risks before starting a task by breaking the work into steps, considering potential hazards, and choosing the safest methods.
This process becomes part of your overall safety program. For example, when installing framing, the analysis covers lifting materials, working near edges, and using tools safely.
The main goal is to ensure everyone knows the job, understands the risks, and uses proper controls before work begins. Software streamlines this by making job safety analysis a repeatable routine for all.
How JSA Construction Software Streamlines the JSA Process
Manual forms make the JSA process slow. A digital tool guides you from draft to review, and stores completed safety documents in one place, reducing paperwork time.
A typical software flow:
- Start with a template.
- Adjust hazards and controls for the task.
- Review, submit, and sign on your phone.
This is the main advantage over paper: less time rewriting forms, more time ensuring control measures fit the job.
Why Construction Sites Are Moving Away from Paper-Based JSAs
Paper forms often get lost in utes, site sheds, or the wrong folder. On busy construction sites, this can slow down job safety steps and make it hard to know which safety analysis form is up to date.
Digital systems help to fix this problem. When a job safety analysis can be made, changed, and signed right from a phone, people are less likely to miss updates or use out-of-date paperwork. This keeps job safety strong on the site.
Common Challenges with Traditional Job Safety Analysis Methods
Traditional work methods create challenges for crews and safety managers. Paper forms are hard to read, easy to lose, and slow to share—especially when plans change.
Common problems include:
- Delays in hazard identification due to missing forms.
- Safety documents scattered across multiple folders.
- Slow approvals that stall the JSA process.
A frequent issue arises when subcontractors bring outdated paper forms. If new hazards exist, teams may begin work without reviewing or acknowledging updated controls.
Main Benefits of Using Digital JSA Construction Software
Digital JSA construction software speeds up processes, provides clearer oversight, and ensures consistency. It enhances workplace safety by making critical information accessible to the right people at the right time.
Key benefits:
- Faster completion with guided templates and fields
- Easy updates to control measures
- Better crew access through mobile-first tools
- Clearer records for safety audits
Most importantly, it saves valuable time. With less admin work, teams can focus on the job site, supporting crews, and ensuring safety controls are followed.
Core Features to Look for in JSA Construction Software
If you are picking job safety analysis software, look for the features that fix problems on site. Don’t be distracted by cool extras that you don’t need. The right digital tool will let your team make, check, update, and find safety documents fast.
Look for:
- Editable templates for different trades and tasks
- Hazard and control libraries so crews aren’t starting from scratch
- Mobile sign-off for review and submission on site
- Version control so everyone works from the current form
- Central storage for easy access during audits
- Offline access for areas with poor reception
Good job hazard analysis software should fit in with how your people already do things. This is very important if you have more than one subcontractor or you run many jobs at the same time.
How JSA Construction Software Improves Site Safety and Compliance
Job safety analysis software helps make construction safety better by making safety protocols simple to follow and show. This is important in the construction industry because lost or old records can lead to big risks.
The software also makes it easier for the team to follow the rules, as all documents will be kept, checked, and changed in a more careful way. When safety processes are clear, people in the team are more likely to do the job the right way.
Conclusion
JSA construction software is essential for modern construction sites, improving job safety and streamlining workflows. Switching from paper to digital tools speeds up safety analysis and boosts productivity while helping teams comply with Australian safety regulations. The software offers digital templates and mobile access, enabling workers to identify and manage risks efficiently on site. As the industry evolves, digital tools safeguard your team and keep projects running smoothly. Make your site safer—try our free trial today!
Frequently Asked Questions
What’s the difference between JSA and SWMS, and when is each used in Australia?
A job safety analysis (JSA) reviews a task, listing steps, hazards, and controls. A safe work method statement (SWMS) is legally required for high-risk construction work—like falls over 2 metres or demolition of load-bearing structures—under WHS Regulations in most Australian states and territories. It must be prepared before work begins. Victoria uses its own OHS Act, so check requirements separately. JSAs are more flexible and can be used for any task. Teams often use both: SWMS for mandated high-risk activities, JSAs for other tasks.
Is JSA construction software suitable for small projects or subcontractors?
Yes, JSA software is useful for small projects too. It streamlines paperwork, speeds up sign-offs, and keeps all safety records organised. Subcontractors benefit from a mobile tool that provides quick access to information on site as they move between jobs.

articles.title: Bentley's first EV is a 375-mile luxury SUV that hits 60 mph in 2.8 seconds
articles.text:
First look: Following months of fervent speculation and multiple official previews, Bentley has finally revealed the Torcal, its first fully electric vehicle. It is the fourth model line in Bentley's current portfolio, joining the Flying Spur luxury sedan, Continental GT/GTC coupe and convertible, and Bentayga SUV.
Like other modern Bentleys, the Torcal is also named after a natural wonder. Bentley says the name comes from El Torcal de Antequera, a natural reserve in the Sierra del Torcal mountains of Andalusia, Spain, known for its striking limestone rock formations, high cliffs, and deep caves.
Designed and engineered at Bentley's headquarters in Crewe in northwest England, the Torcal SUV is based on the Porsche Cayenne Electric's 800-volt PPE platform. However, while the Cayenne EV delivers around 1,156 hp and 1,106 lb-ft of torque in its flagship Turbo variant, the Torcal focuses more on luxury and offers relatively restrained performance.
The Torcal is available in two trims: a base Core model and a sportier S variant. Both feature a 113.2 kWh battery that Bentley claims delivers an estimated range of up to 375 miles on the WLTP cycle, or around 320 miles under EPA testing. The battery supports up to 400 kW of DC fast charging, which can charge it from 10% to 80% in just 16 minutes or add 100 miles of range in just seven minutes.
In terms of performance, both the Core and S trims feature the same dual-motor permanent-magnet synchronous powertrain with an all-wheel-drive layout. In the flagship Torcal S, the setup delivers up to 888 PS (876 hp) of power and 1,350 Nm (996 lb-ft) of torque, while the Core variant delivers 821 PS (810 hp) and 1,194 Nm (852 lb-ft) of torque.
Bentley claims 0-60 mph acceleration times of 3.3 seconds for the Torcal Core and 2.8 seconds for the Torcal S. The former can reach a top speed of 155 mph, while the latter can reach up to 162 mph. It is worth noting that the Torcal S was tested with Launch Control enabled, while the Core does not offer the feature.
The Torcal Core starts at £165,000 in the UK and $230,000 in the US, while the Torcal S starts at a cool £200,000/$270,000. Bentley will start accepting pre-orders next month, but production is not scheduled to begin until Q2 2027. Alongside the US and UK, the Torcal has been confirmed to launch in Germany, Switzerland, Canada, China, India, and other major markets.

articles.title: PrismML brings its tiny LLMs to Qualcomm-powered smart glasses | TechCrunch
articles.text:
The AI Lab PrismML — founded by Caltech researchers and advised by UC Berkeley’s Ion Stoica — has created a version of its tiny language models for smart glasses running on Qualcomm’s Snapdragon chips.
On Wednesday, at Qualcomm’s Snapdragon Summit, the chipmaker showcased PrismML’s 1-bit Bonsai LLM, which can be run locally on AI smart glasses built on the Snapdragon AR1 Gen 1 Platform.
As TechCrunch previously reported, PrismML’s claim to fame is that it shrinks larger models substantially (in this case, by 4x), while retaining almost all of their performance on standard benchmarks. The smart glasses version is a 2-billion-parameter model tuned for vision and language, so wearers can ask what they’re looking at in real time.
Prism’s larger goal is open-weight AI that runs on devices and makes better use of the computing power they already have. The startup pitches this as an alternative to depending on the privacy promises of proprietary AI labs and their insatiable need for more compute.
Releasing a model for Qualcomm’s chip is a step toward that vision. But no smart glasses running PrismML have been announced yet.

articles.title: Donald Duck's uncle was partly based on Wernher von Braun
articles.text:
Did you know that the first character that Walt Disney created to specifically appear on television was inspired, in part, by early Space Age rocket scientists?
On this day 65 years ago (September 24, 1961), Disney introduced the “renowned scientist, lecturer, psychologist [and] world traveler,” Ludwig Von Drake. A member of the Duck family (he is the “brilliant and eccentric” uncle of Donald Duck), Von Drake was “the outstanding genius of the century” (per Disney himself) who helped to explain scientific principles and technological concepts to the millions of people who tuned in every Sunday to watch Walt Disney’s Wonderful World of Color on NBC.
A few years later, after expertly (but often absent-mindedly) addressing topics such as how color television works, the health benefits of exercising, and the history of aviation, Von Drake dove into the topic for which he said he wrote the book on, in the February 10, 1963, episode “Inside Outer Space.”
“You people out there are going to see stars you have never seen before… when you go traveling in outer space. In fact, there are going to be a lot of things out there you don’t know about, but don’t let it bother you, ’cause all of the answers is [sic] right in here,” Von Drake says at the beginning of the animated segment. “I call my guidebook Inside Outer Space because everything known about outer space is on the inside.
“Which reminds me, the way things are going, you better get your copy right away before it becomes obsolete,” he says. “And prices go up.”
Tomorrowland
As it turns out, Von Drake was not wrong—well, maybe not about the cost of his book, but about the part about being obsolete. The show reused animation from earlier Disneyland TV episodes, “Man and the Moon,” “Man in Space,” and “Mars and Beyond,” which first aired on December 4, 1957, two months after the launch of the world’s first artificial satellite.

Founded in 2015 and headquartered in Shenzhen, SKYEAST is a professional company engaged in electronic component sourcing and distribution. We work with renowned semiconductor brands worldwide, dedicating ourselves to providing comprehensive, high-quality, and efficient products and services to our customers.
In a market defined by volatility, inventory is leverage. When the manufacturer raises prices, buyers who stocked up early hold the advantage — and the gap between contract pricing and spot availability often decides whether a production line keeps running.
SKYEAST currently holds over $30 million in ready stock, covering industrial, automotive, AI, and other key applications. TI sits at the core of our product line, supported by ADI and MAXIM as key brands, covering analog, signal processing, and power management components across the full range of mainstream demand — serving R&D and mass production across industrial control, automotive electronics, smart devices, consumer electronics, and more.
We operate dual warehouses in Shenzhen and Hong Kong, with business reaching markets across the US, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Japan, Singapore, Australia, Canada, and beyond. Our product portfolio spans everything from 3C to industrial, automotive, and medical electronics, from basic to core components — meeting the diverse procurement needs of our customers.
But depth of stock is only half the story. What matters just as much is how that stock is managed. Our rolling pre-stock programs are built around each customer’s production plan, positioning inventory ahead of demand rather than chasing after it. For buyers who have watched one shipment slip too many times, that difference is everything.
The point isn’t simply having parts. It’s having the right parts, in the right place, at the right time.
Response Speed Is the Real Differentiator
In a fast-moving market, how quickly a supplier responds can matter more than the price itself. A quote that arrives two days late is a quote that arrives after the decision has already been made.
SKYEAST commits to quotes within two hours, with 7×24 online inquiry support across all time zones. For overseas buyers, that means no waiting overnight for a reply, no missed windows, and no guessing games while a competitor moves first.
And for orders placed before October 31st, we are holding quotes valid for a full week — giving buyers the room to plan, compare, and commit without being chased by a price that shifts by the hour.
Around our customers’ needs, we have built five core services: Global Strategic Solutions, Quick Inventory Response Support, Quality Inspection Services, Replacement Selection Support, and Financial Support Services. From component selection to delivery, from technical coordination to financial arrangements — one-stop coverage that makes procurement simple.
Trust Built on Consistency, Not Promises
In a rising market, the two things buyers care about most are the two things we take most seriously.
The first is price stability. When the manufacturer raises prices, many suppliers pass that increase straight through — sometimes mid-order, sometimes onto customers who had already agreed to terms. SKYEAST does not. We do not raise prices on contract customers simply because the manufacturer did. An order placed is an order honored.
The second is quality. Every shipment passes through a full-process inspection by our independent quality department, operating under an ISO9001-certified system. Products are checked for appearance, performance, and parameter accuracy, and every batch is traceable and verifiable. It is this discipline that has kept us at a zero major quality incident record — and kept our customers coming back.
That record was not built overnight. Over the years, SKYEAST has served more than 5,000 customers, with over 3,000 long-term partners who return order after order. In an industry where suppliers come and go with every market cycle, that kind of consistency says more than any advertisement could.
A Partner for the Long Run
Behind our service capability sits a stable and carefully built supply chain. We work closely with original manufacturers and have established long-term strategic relationships with experienced solution providers and spot suppliers across the domestic market. That foundation allows us to keep supply stable, pricing transparent, and lead times controllable — responding quickly to market shifts and customer demand alike.
Our vision is to be the preferred integrated service provider of electronic components for our global customers. Our mission is to provide global customers with the highest quality electronic components distribution services, improve the efficiency of global electronic intelligence, and promote technological progress and social development. Embrace change, honest and upright, optimistic and never give up, professional and persistent — these are not slogans on a wall, but what we do every day.
Beyond supply, we offer the kind of support that turns a vendor into a partner: component selection guidance, solution optimization, and technical coordination, all designed to lower R&D costs and shorten time to market. For customers navigating a price increase while trying to hit a launch date, that combination is what truly works.
The Window Is Open Now
The October price adjustment is coming. Buyers who prepare now will be the ones who stay ahead — and buyers who wait will be the ones paying spot premiums later.
If you are sourcing TI or ADI components and want to lock in stable supply before the market moves, now is the time to reach out. We are online around the clock, and we will get you a quote within two hours.
SKYEAST — your reliable global IC distribution and solution partner.

articles.title: After IonQ Buyout, SkyWater Reiterates Role as Quantum Foundry - EE Times
articles.text:
After quantum computing company IonQ acquired SkyWater in July this year, the subsidiary said it is pledging to treat its quantum chip customers equally, including parent IonQ.
“IonQ is treated as a customer of the foundry, just like anyone else,” SkyWater’s new SVP of quantum technologies Mihir Bhaskar told EE Times. “For all quantum customers SkyWater serves, their data and information remain strictly with the dedicated SkyWater team manufacturing their devices.”
Bhaskar, a quantum technologist for 15 years, founded Lightsynq, specializing in photonic interconnects and quantum memory, in 2024. IonQ acquired the company in 2025.
“Since joining IonQ, I’ve helped lead technology strategy, including assisting with the acquisition of SkyWater,” Bhaskar said. “With SkyWater now in place, the most exciting role for me is leading the SkyWater Quantum Solutions business unit to support all our quantum customers.”
SkyWater has nine “major” quantum customers, according to Bhaskar. Startup competitor Anderon has parent IBM as its primary customer and is looking for more.
“Priority number one for any business—especially in the foundry space—is protecting customer intellectual property,” Bhaskar said. “If your customers don’t trust you, you can’t do business. It is critical in the foundry business because customers bring highly sensitive IP and designs, trusting us to manufacture them.”
SkyWater has been making quantum chips for about 10 years. Its customers include IonQ, PsiQuantum, Qolab, and QuamCore.
Qolab and QuamCore are building what Bhaskar described as “potentially disruptive” superconducting technologies that may eliminate the well-known “chandelier” design from quantum computers.
“A major challenge in scaling superconducting qubit systems used by players like IBM, Google, and Rigetti is wiring and controlling larger numbers of qubits without creating a massive, tangled mess of cables,” Bhaskar said. “SkyWater is building a platform with Quadcore to solve these high-density integration and routing challenges.”
Modalities
The “modalities”, or techniques, that quantum chip companies use to make qubits include trapped ions, quantum dots, silicon vacancies in diamond, photonics, and superconducting.
Bhaskar said every one of those modalities ultimately relies on either superconducting or photonic methods to move quantum information.
“We support all major modalities,” Bhaskar said. “That might sound impossible for a single foundry, but fundamentally, there are only two ways to transport quantum information across a chip or system.”
SkyWater offers its SC250 (superconducting) and SP90 (photonics) platforms together with its technology-as-a-service model that provides early-stage process customization to prove manufacturability.
“While we offer baseline process design kit platforms [PDKs], our core business model accommodates custom process development within a volume manufacturing environment,” Bhaskar said. “We develop new processes outside standard PDKs to make breakthrough innovations manufacturable for the first time.”
Anderon
IBM established Anderon with the help of the U.S. government in May this year as the “world’s first” pure-play quantum chip foundry. The U.S. Department of Commerce awarded Anderon $1 billion under the CHIPS Act early in September to scale production. IBM is Anderon’s main customer.
Specific to the U.S., additional domestic capacity can help address supply chain constraints, provide manufacturing redundancy, and give quantum companies more options as they move from research prototypes toward production, Heather West, IDC’s quantum research lead, told EE Times.
Anderon offers customers wafers supporting superconducting qubit arrays, quantum input/output signaling, and readout signal chain components, new CEO Mukesh Khare told EE Times. The company plans to expand to other quantum modalities, such as spin qubits, he said.
“Fantastic step”
U.S. government investment in domestic quantum semiconductor manufacturing is a “fantastic step” for the entire ecosystem, Bhaskar said.
“Competitors like Anderon are building new 300-mm facilities for future capability,” Bhaskar noted.
SkyWater supplies its quantum customers from two 200-mm facilities in Minnesota and Florida as well as a 300-mm advanced packaging facility in Florida for chiplet integration and new materials.
“SkyWater is already shipping quantum wafers today and has been doing so for the last decade,” Bhaskar noted. “Our active capacity has powered the last several generations of quantum innovation and will continue to power the next. While others are working toward becoming a quantum foundry in the future, SkyWater is already the operational quantum foundry today.”

articles.title: Kein Handy, keine Karte: Revolut macht das Gesicht zum Zahlungsmittel
articles.text:
Kein Handy, keine Karte: Revolut macht das Gesicht zum Zahlungsmittel
Revolut erprobt derzeit in Großbritannien mit „Pay with Smile“ ein neues Bezahlverfahren, das in ausgewählten Filialen der Kaffeekette Kiss the Hippo getestet wird. Dabei hinterlegt der Kunde einen Gesichtsscan und verknüpft diesen mit seinem Revolut-Konto. An der Kasse erkennt eine Kamera das Gesicht, ordnet es dem Revolut-Konto zu und löst die Zahlung über Revolut Pay aus. Für die Nutzer:innen ergeben sich im Rahmen des Pilotversuchs spezielle Sonderangebote, die ausschließlich über diesen Zahlungsweg beglichen werden können und zusätzliche Punkte bringen.
Es muss also werder eine physische Karte aufgelegt noch eingesteckt werden, auch eine Auslösung per Smartphone oder Wearable ist nicht erforderlich. Das Gesicht wird so zum alleinigen Auslöser der Zahlung. Denn üblicherweise wird Revolut Pay am Terminal per NFC oder QR-Code gestartet und dann in der Revolut-App bestätigt.
Auch wenn der Kunde oder die Kundin für Pay with Smile ein Revolut-Konto benötigen, ist es keine spezielle Visa- oder Mastercard-bezogene Funktion, sondern ein Element, das an das Revolut-Konto selbst in Kombination mit den unternehmenseigenen Kassensystemen gebunden ist. Dabei setzt das System die Hardware Revolut Register voraus, ein Kassensystem mit zwei Bildschirmen. Vom Einsatz her könnte ein solches System gut in Kantinen oder anderen halbgeschlossenen Systemen, wo Kund:innen sich besonders regelmäßig aufhalten, zum Einsatz kommen.
Händler haben keinen Zugang zu biometrischen Daten
Der Regelbetrieb ist zwar noch nicht gesichert, aber das Unternehmen macht schon deutlich, dass die Händler für die Lösung keine Extragebühren zahlen müssen, die über die übliche Abwicklung hinausgehen. Datenschutztechnisch betont das Unternehmen, dass eine Ende-zu-Ende-Verschlüsselung stattfindet, sodass keinerlei zusätzliche Daten biometrischer Natur für den Handel zugänglich sein werden.
Die Bezahllösung klingt zunächst erstrebenswert: man benötigt weder seine Karte noch den Geldbeutel und muss sich keine PIN merken, es reicht der Blick zur Kasse, was gerade in Stoßzeiten den Bezahlvorgang beschleunigen kann, wenn der Workflow erst einmal gelernt ist. Unklar ist, was passiert, wenn mehrere Personen, die das System verwenden, in der Kassenzone stehen.
Andererseits könnten Kund:innen mit der Biometrie ein Problem haben – denn gerade Gesichtsdaten sind besonders sensible persönliche Daten. Ob der Pilotversuch, der in Großbritannien stattfindet, auch im Rahmen der DSGVO für Deutschland und den EU-Raum umzusetzen wäre, ist zu prüfen. Immerhin nutzt Revolut aber Gesichtserkennung bereits für andere Identitätsprüfungen und nennt dort ausdrücklich die Einwilligung als Rechtsgrundlage für die Verarbeitung biometrischer Daten.
Letztlich könnte das Bezahlverfahren für Revolut aber noch aus dem Ökosystemgedanken heraus interessant sein, denn strategisch ist es mehr als ein reines Nice-to-Have-Feature, weil das Unternehmen so versucht, Konto, Payment Scheme, Händler-Acquiring, Kasse und Identifikation zusammen zu führen.

articles.title: From tokenmaxxing to context engineering: Why enterprise AI needs better context, not bigger prompts
articles.text:
Elastic
View Brand Publisher
From tokenmaxxing to context engineering: Why enterprise AI needs better context, not bigger prompts
Drawing on Elastic's experience helping enterprises build AI for production, Head of Field Engineering Ravindra Ramnani explains why context engineering is emerging as the next critical discipline for enterprise AI.
For a while, enterprise AI seemed to have a simple rule: if a model could process more information, it would produce better answers. As context windows expanded from thousands of tokens to millions, bigger numbers became synonymous with progress, and in response, organisations fed AI assistants entire document repositories and conversation histories.
At Elastic, this shift was evident as customers moved from pilot programs into production. The challenge was never whether AI could handle more data, but whether it was reasoning over the right data.
Tokenmaxxing began as a Silicon Valley workplace trend in early 2026: maximising AI token consumption as a signal of productivity. Some companies built internal leaderboards ranking employees by tokens burned, and high usage became a status symbol regardless of output quality. The trend drew sharp criticism because it measures inputs, not outcomes. “It is the AI-era equivalent of judging developers by lines of code," as Ravindra Ramnani, Head of Field Engineering, India, Elastic puts it.
The same fallacy shows up at the architecture level, where teams include irrelevant documents and conversation histories in prompts, assuming more information improves output. Models don’t filter unnecessary material like skilled analysts, resulting in more noise, slower responses, and outputs needing significant human review.
The gap became clear once organisations moved into production, where an agent acting on incomplete context doesn't just cost more; it produces consequential errors. "The conversation therefore shifted from 'how much can we give the model' to 'what does the model actually need to know.' That question lies at the heart of context engineering," says Ramnani.
What context engineering actually means
Context engineering is the discipline of deciding what a model sees at each step of its reasoning: which instructions frame the task, which tools are available, what is retrieved from enterprise systems, what is carried forward from earlier turns, and what is deliberately left out. In enterprise settings, the hardest part is retrieval, because the model has to be grounded in trusted internal knowledge without getting buried in it.
A simple analogy helps. Tokenmaxxing is handing someone an entire filing cabinet and asking them to find the relevant page. Context engineering is handing them the three pages they actually need, already tabbed. Both offer the same information. Only one enables better decisions.
Relevance isn't simply a search feature, either. It's the mechanism that makes autonomous AI safe to act on. When an agent reasons from incomplete data, the risk isn't just wasted compute. In a banking compliance workflow or a security operations centre, a wrong autonomous action can propagate before a human has a chance to intervene. The right information needs to be smaller in volume, higher in signal, and permission-controlled, so an agent only accesses what it's authorised to use. That combination of relevance and governance separates a reliable production agent from an expensive pilot.
How Elastic approaches it
Effective context engineering rests on three layers: data proximity, keeping the reasoning layer close to the source of truth rather than routing sensitive data through external pipelines; retrieval precision, surfacing only what is genuinely signal for a given decision, where Elastic's hybrid search, combining vector, keyword, and structured retrieval with semantic reranking, ensures what reaches the model is relevant rather than merely related; and execution grounding, loading agent capabilities on demand rather than arming every agent with a full toolkit on every turn, which reduces both token overhead and the risk of unintended autonomous action.
Elastic brings retrieval, tool creation, conversational grounding, and agent observability into a single platform, with the ability to deploy entirely on-premises or in air-gapped environments, and techniques like Better Binary Quantisation that reduce the vector memory footprint of retrieval data by up to 32 times while preserving accuracy.
This is also a business question before it's an engineering one: business teams need to define what good looks like before technical teams build for it, or organisations end up with elegant pipelines feeding agents the wrong data.
The impact is clearest in high-stakes decisions: security analysts getting only signals relevant to a specific threat rather than a generic feed, Financial Services and Insurance (FSI) teams grounding agents in the regulatory context of a transaction where CERT-In's 12-hour window and RBI frameworks create real pressure, and Global Capability Centres (GCC) developers getting answers grounded in their organisation's own systems. These use cases are particularly relevant in India, where enterprises operate across diverse data environments spanning legacy core banking systems and modern cloud-native applications, often with Hindi and regional-language records. With DPDP Act obligations and data localisation expectations, running the full AI stack on-premises or in air-gapped environments isn't a preference for many organisations, but a procurement requirement.
The most common mistake is assuming that connecting a model to enterprise data is the same as grounding it in enterprise context, since access doesn't guarantee relevant retrieval; a close second is treating agent observability as optional, leaving organisations unable to explain agent decisions to regulators.
Model selection will matter far less than the quality of context a model reasons over. A well-grounded smaller model consistently outperforms a larger model working from fragmented context, and competitive advantage is shifting away from model procurement, accessible to everyone at broadly comparable cost, toward the intelligence layer that determines what any model can actually know and do.
Enterprises also need to rethink how they measure AI success. Token usage and model size reveal little about business value. More meaningful measures are outcome-oriented: task completion rate against how often a human has to override it, decision accuracy in production versus testing, time-to-answer in high-stakes workflows, and regulatory auditability, an explainable record of what data an agent consulted and why.
Gartner projects that by the end of 2026, 40% of enterprise applications will incorporate task-specific agents, and systems without a unified, trusted data foundation don't just inherit the risks of individual agents; they compound them.
The organisations that extract the most durable value from AI won't be those that deployed earliest or chose the most sophisticated model. They will be those that invested in making their enterprise knowledge accessible, accurate, and trustworthy so that any reasoning system can act on it with confidence.
The model is not the moat. The data foundation is.

articles.title: Batalla campal en una boda en Orense: la novia exige 40.000 euros al novio, le es infiel en los baños y la Guardia Civil tiene que intervenir
articles.text:
Algunas películas acaban en boda y algunas bodas acaban de película. Concretamente, de cine bélico. Una boda celebrada el pasado sábado en el municipio de Gomesende (Ourense) ha terminado como el rosario de la Aurora: banquete interrumpido, vajilla hecha añicos, una presunta infidelidad en los baños del local y la intervención de la Guardia Civil para separar a dos familias enfrentadas a golpes. Cuatro días después, el propio novio ha salido a desmentir parte de la historia y a asegurar que la pareja sigue junta y feliz. Si esto fuera un relato salvaje de los que se cuentan en los bares, ya tendría secuelas aseguradas: ‘La boda de Gomesende 2: la venganza de la vajilla’.
El escenario. El enlace tuvo lugar en A Casa da Tulla, una casona del siglo XVII situada muy cerca de la frontera con Portugal y un lugar que sus usuarios destacan por sus vistas y su tranquilidad. Los protagonistas son un vecino del municipio de Ramirás y una mujer de origen colombiano, que habían decidido formalizar su relación con una boda que debía ser un día idílico en un enclave de ensueño. En cualquier película romántica, aquí vendría el montaje con fotos en blanco y negro y la música de piano. En esta, el guion decidió saltar directamente a la tercera parte.
Según el relato publicado por La Región, el amor no era precisamente el ingrediente principal de la celebración: durante el mismo banquete, la recién casada exigió a su marido 40.000 euros procedentes de un supuesto pacto nupcial, una cifra que debía salir de los regalos aportados por los invitados, tal y como recogió también ABC en su cobertura del suceso. Irónicamente, esto es lo que cuesta de media una boda.
La chispa. La negativa del novio a entregar el dinero encendió la mecha. En la discusión mediaron los hermanos de la novia y la hermana del novio, pero en lugar de calmar la situación, el enfrentamiento escaló: varios invitados terminaron tirándose de los pelos y propinándose golpes e insultos entre ambos bandos familiares. Más que un vals aquí pega heavy metal.
El resultado fue un auténtico "espectáculo desagradable" que dejó vajilla rota y otros desperfectos menores, además de gran parte de la factura del convite todavía sin abonar. La violencia alcanzó tal nivel que obligó a intervenir a la Guardia Civil, que se desplazó hasta el recinto para levantar acta de lo sucedido.
El affaire. O un “rápido desahogo carnal”, mejor dicho. Mientras las familias se enzarzaban, la novia se retiró en algún momento de la celebración a los baños del local junto a un joven que había participado en la organización del evento. Mantuvieron un breve encuentro sexual y siguieron como si nada. “Me llevé a un guapo al baño”, confiesa. La propia novia habría reconocido después ante sus amigos que había bebido mucho durante la fiesta, que no sentía nada por su flamante marido y que ya había puesto el asunto en manos de su abogado para tramitar un divorcio inmediato.
El novio, por su parte, se oponía a cualquier acuerdo de ruptura y le pedía que siguieran juntos. Pero sus familiares, muy conocidos en Ramirás (su pueblo natural, de 2100 habitantes), asistieron atónitos al espectáculo protagonizado por su hijo y decidieron romper toda relación con él. Además, pidió al resto de familiares que no le entregaran ningún dinero, culpándolo de "mala cabeza" y de haber entrado en una relación que solo le iba a traer problemas, según el reportaje original.
El giro. Cuatro días después del suceso, el novio decidió romper su silencio con un mensaje propio publicado en Atlántico, en el que ofrece una versión radicalmente distinta. El plot twist: nunca existió un acuerdo económico de 40.000 euros vinculado a la boda, tampoco hubo infidelidad alguna y, sobre todo, él y su esposa "no nos separamos en ningún momento" durante la celebración.
Eso sí, el novio admite que hubo enfrentamientos, aunque habla de dos peleas distintas: la primera se originó cuando su hermana, que está enferma, tapó la boca a su mujer mientras esta hablaba, un gesto ante el que reaccionó el hermano de la novia y que derivó en el primer altercado. La segunda, que califica como "más gorda", enfrentó a dos invitadas que se agarraron del pelo fuera del recinto. Si esto fuera una saga, aquí llegaría el flashback explicativo.
"Nunca dejaré que se manche el nombre de nuestras familias", sentencia el novio que, según su versión, tanto él como su mujer se encuentran actualmente instalados en A Coruña, donde ambos estarían trabajando con normalidad, lejos ya del foco mediático que ha convertido su boda en Gomesende en un drama viral.

articles.title: Des drones aux sous-marins, Airbus va protéger les communications secrètes de l'armée française
articles.text:
Les armées françaises empilent les réseaux comme d’autres empilent les étages : chaque niveau de classification, du non protégé au secret, vit derrière ses propres murs. Le moindre fichier qui passe d’un étage à l’autre représente un risque. Le 23 septembre, la DGA a notifié à Airbus le contrat PARACOM, qui organise ces échanges pour les 25 prochaines années, pour un montant non communiqué.
Une écluse numérique entre le secret et le reste du monde
Le contrat porte sur des passerelles de cybersécurité, des équipements dont le métier consiste à autoriser des échanges « sécurisés et filtrés » entre des systèmes de sensibilités différentes. L’image la plus parlante reste celle du poste-frontière : tout ce qui veut passer d’un réseau à l’autre est contrôlé, filtré, et rien ne circule en dehors de ce point de passage. Les passerelles d’Airbus sont homologuées pour relier des réseaux allant du niveau « secret » au non classifié.
Lire aussi : Airbus choisit Mistral AI pour propulser l’IA dans ses avions et ses systèmes de défense
La gamme se décline en trois familles : des versions en rack pour les centres de données, des unités autonomes pour les postes de commandement, et des variantes pour les usages tactiques. Le marché couvre l’ensemble du cycle de vie de ces équipements : conception, développement, production, puis maintien en condition sur la durée. Le périmètre de déploiement donne la mesure du programme, des bâtiments de surface aux sous-marins, en passant par les avions, les hélicoptères, les drones et les blindés. « Cette passerelle renforce le bouclier numérique sur lequel les armées françaises s’appuient pour conduire leurs missions », résume François Lombard, directeur de l’intelligence connectée d’Airbus Defence and Space.
Airbus, fournisseur des armées depuis plus de 10 ans
Depuis 2013, l’armée de terre s’équipe déjà en passerelles Airbus ; PARACOM étend le principe à l’ensemble des armées et de leurs plateformes. La durée interpelle davantage : vingt-cinq ans, dans la tech civile, tiennent de l’ère géologique (le Wi-Fi grand public n’a pas trente ans). L’échelle militaire raisonne autrement : un sous-marin ou un avion de combat reste en service plusieurs décennies, et les équipements qui protègent leurs communications doivent suivre le même rythme.
Le montant, lui, restera dans l’ombre, comme souvent pour ce type de contrat de défense. En creux, le programme dit surtout la place prise par la cyberdéfense dans l’équipement des armées, à l’heure où tout se connecte, du drone au blindé, et où chaque liaison ajoutée devient une porte de plus à surveiller.

articles.title: Australia investiga si el hackeo de un agente de OpenAI a un sitio de salud pública violó la ley
articles.text:
El gobierno de Australia abrió una investigación para determinar si un agente de inteligencia artificial de OpenAI violó la ley al infiltrarse en un portal público de salud y acceder durante meses a datos internos sin autorización.
El primer ministro, Anthony Albanese, reveló el hackeo en Nueva York, durante la Asamblea General de la ONU, y dijo que habrá “obviamente consecuencias legales” para la empresa.
PUBLICIDAD
Tres meses sin aviso oficial a Australia
Según Albanese, el agente ingresó el 18 de junio de 2026, al Medicare Statistics Reporting Service, el portal público que administra Services Australia con estadísticas agregadas del sistema de salud universal del país, conocido como Medicare.
OpenAI recién detectó el incidente en agosto de 2026, durante una revisión interna más amplia sobre agentes que actuaban de forma no prevista, según un vocero de la compañía a TechCrunch.
La empresa notificó a Services Australia el 10 de septiembre de 2026, con un correo enviado a la casilla pública del organismo. Cinco días después, esa misma entidad alertó al Centro de Seguridad Cibernética del gobierno.
PUBLICIDAD
“Esta situación es obviamente inaceptable”, dijo Albanese ante la prensa y agregó que había hablado directamente con el director ejecutivo de OpenAI, Sam Altman, para transmitirle la “extrema preocupación” de Australia.
Un agente de OpenAI que no aceptó un no
El primer ministro explicó que el agente buscaba información pública sobre gasto en medicamentos cuando encontró una manera de esquivar los bloqueos de seguridad del portal.
“El agente de IA encontró una forma de evadir esos bloqueos, no aceptó un no como respuesta”, relató Albanese, y precisó que no hay evidencia de que se haya filtrado información personal de ciudadanos.
El viceprimer ministro, Richard Marles, calificó el episodio como el primer caso conocido de un agente de IA con acceso no autorizado a los sistemas informáticos del gobierno australiano. “Esto es una advertencia sobre una tecnología que se desarrolla sin las protecciones necesarias”, dijo.
PUBLICIDAD
Marles agregó que la información obtenida estaba en el “extremo menos sensible” y que ya fue hecha pública, aunque remarcó que la preocupación central es que la intrusión no fue solicitada ni prevista por nadie.
La ministra de Servicios Gubernamentales, Katy Gallagher, confirmó que el portal fue cerrado y que los datos se trasladaron a sistemas más seguros. Según Albanese, otros tres organismos podrían haber sido afectados: el Instituto Australiano de Salud y Bienestar, la oficina de estadísticas de Nueva Gales del Sur y el Departamento de Salud de Victoria.
Qué investigará el gobierno de Australia
La pesquisa estará a cargo del departamento del primer ministro, con apoyo de la Dirección de Señales de Australia, la agencia de ciberseguridad e inteligencia electrónica del país y del Instituto de Seguridad de IA.
PUBLICIDAD
Albanese afirmó que la revisión analizará si hubo una violación de la ley vigente y si el marco legal actual está preparado para una tecnología de IA capaz de actuar de forma autónoma. También, se investigará por qué las agencias de seguridad australianas no detectaron la intrusión antes del aviso de OpenAI.
En un comunicado, OpenAI indicó que lleva adelante una “revisión exhaustiva de actividad de modelos desalineada” durante el entrenamiento y la evaluación, y que notifica a terceros cuando identifica un impacto potencial en sus sistemas. La empresa explicó que sus modelos “tomaron acciones que no fueron intencionadas” mientras buscaban estadísticas sobre Australia.
PUBLICIDAD
El episodio se conoció horas después de que Altman advirtiera, en el Consejo de Seguridad de la ONU, sobre el riesgo de que la IA avance “tan rápido que las personas ya no puedan seguir lo que pasa ni intervenir cuando sea necesario”.
Medios australianos como ABC News reportaron que la intrusión en Medicare podría estar vinculada a un incidente previo en el que agentes de OpenAI habían accedido sin autorización a una wiki alemana, usada como punto de partida para dejar notas sobre cómo atacar sistemas del gobierno australiano.
El gobierno todavía no confirmó si habrá cargos penales contra la empresa. Albanese dijo que la investigación determinará qué consecuencias legales corresponden y si el episodio, calificado por él mismo como algo “sin precedentes”, requiere una nueva regulación específica para agentes de IA.
PUBLICIDAD
PUBLICIDAD
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: Depois do Windows, Qualcomm agora aposta no Linux • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Depois do Windows, Qualcomm agora aposta no Linux
Qualcomm anunciou suporte oficial ao Linux em computadores equipados com chips Snapdragon X2.
A Qualcomm introduziu os chips Snapdragon X em 2023 com a missão de fazer a arquitetura Arm ganhar espaço no segmento de PCs. Mas o foco sempre esteve no ecossistema do Windows. Até agora: a companhia acaba de anunciar o suporte ao Linux em computadores baseados na série Snapdragon X2.
É verdade que este é um “Early Developer Preview”, ou seja, o projeto está em fase de prévia para desenvolvedores. Isso significa que a novidade não é interessante para usuários “normais” no atual estágio. Atualmente, o objetivo é permitir que desenvolvedores criem, testem e otimizem software para Linux nessas máquinas.
Não é que já não fosse possível rodar Linux em notebooks equipados com processadores Snapdragon X. Isso é feito, essencialmente, via implementação ARM64 (AArch64) do kernel. O problema é que é preciso também oferecer suporte a componentes relacionados à CPU, como a GPU e a NPU. Sem apoio do fabricante, a comunidade Linux tem que se virar para isso.
O anúncio da Qualcomm chama a atenção porque, nele, a companhia afirma que está trabalhando para tornar os componentes relacionados à série Snapdragon X2 compatíveis com o Linux diretamente no nível do kernel, sem que esse suporte precise ser oferecido por meio de patches não oficiais e afins.
Por exemplo: o suporte às GPUs Adreno será feito por meio dos projetos Freedreno, Turnip e Rusticl (OpenGL, Vulkan e OpenCL). Outro: o suporte às NPUs Hexagon será feito via projeto FastRPC para permitir a execução plena de tarefas locais de IA.
Em linhas gerais, estamos falando de um trabalho extenso, mas que está em andamento, segundo a própria empresa:
O suporte para Linux em laptops com Snapdragon da série X2 está sendo implementado em etapas, começando com os componentes principais que os desenvolvedores precisam antes de poderem trabalhar em nível de produção em seus dispositivos.
(…) Com essas bases estabelecidas, os desenvolvedores terão um caminho mais claro para criar, testar e otimizar aplicativos em hardware real, em vez de apenas validar se o Linux inicializa.
Qualcomm
A Qualcomm ainda não deu uma data para isso. Mas, de acordo com o cronograma divulgado pela companhia, o plano é tornar o projeto estável o suficiente para ele sair da fase “preview” até o fim de novembro de 2026.
Depois disso, a Qualcomm pretende ampliar o suporte oferecendo códigos-fonte atualizados, drivers, imagens, documentação e afins, sempre tendo como base o Debian 13 “Trixie”, distribuição que tem servido de referência para esses esforços. Aliás, o trabalho feito até agora já está disponível no GitHub.
É de se presumir que o projeto será verdadeiramente acessível a usuários de todos os níveis a partir do primeiro semestre de 2027, quando fabricantes como Asus e HP oferecerão suporte oficial ao Linux em notebooks com Snapdragon X2. No mesmo ano, a Canonical pretende lançar uma versão do Ubuntu certificada para esses chips.
Fica a torcida para que o envolvimento da Qualcomm com o Linux seja mantido em séries de chips sucessoras, é claro.

Annoncée en juin 2026, la fonction Moods permet d’appliquer des styles générés par IA, inspirés notamment des pellicules 35 mm et des appareils photo numériques des années 2000. Une nouveauté qui s’accompagne de plusieurs améliorations dont un outil d’annotation capable de masquer des informations sensibles ou encore de nouveaux modèles pour sa fonction Remix.

Vos photos, vos effets
